1: # Copilot Instructions — QBrainAi
2: 
3: **Agent Identity:** When posting to the MCP session log, use the agent's actual identity in Pascal-Case for `sourceType` and the session ID prefix. Do not use inaccurate aliases, lowercase names, or legacy placeholders. Example: `Codex`.
4: For specific operational instructions (session bootstrap, turn logging lifecycle, helper command order), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
5: 
6: ## Response Formatting
7: 
8: - Do not use table-style output in responses.
9: - Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.
10: 
11: ## Terminal Usage
12: 
13: - Do NOT set focus to the terminal window.
14: - Do NOT write multiline commands to the terminal; use temporary scripts instead.
15: - Use **only `pwsh.exe`** (PowerShell 7+). Do not invoke `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) for scripts, examples, or tooling.
16: 
17: ## Session Logging Requirements
18: 
19: - Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for workflow and helper command order.
20: - Persist session log changes immediately after each meaningful update; do not batch unsaved turn changes.
21: - For each turn, include as much detail as available: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), files modified, design decisions, requirements discovered, blockers, and context references.
22: 
23: ## Build, Test, Lint
24: 
25: ```powershell
26: # Build (via Nuke)
27: ./build.ps1 Compile
28: # or: dotnet build src\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp -c Debug
29: 
30: # Run all unit tests (via Nuke)
31: ./build.ps1 Test
32: # or individual projects:
33: # dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug
34: # dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Client.Tests -c Debug
35: # dotnet test tests\Build.Tests -c Debug
36: 
37: # Run integration tests (uses CustomWebApplicationFactory, in-memory EF)
38: dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests -c Debug
39: 
40: # Run a single test by fully-qualified name
41: dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests.QueryAsync_NoFilters_ReturnsAllItems"
42: 
43: # Run tests in a single class
44: dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests"
45: 
46: # Validate appsettings config (via Nuke)
47: ./build.ps1 ValidateConfig
48: # or: pwsh.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ./scripts/Validate-McpConfig.ps1
49: 
50: # Validate requirements traceability
51: ./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability
52: 
53: # Markdown lint (docs only)
54: # CI uses markdownlint-cli2 with .markdownlint-cli2.yaml
55: ```
56: 
57: ## Architecture
58: 
59: **QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:
60: 
61: - **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
62: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
63: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.
64: 
65: **Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.
66: 
67: **Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.
68: 
69: **Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.
70: 
71: **Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.
72: 
73: ## Key Conventions
74: 
75: ### XML Documentation Required
76: 
77: `TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.
78: 
79: ### Requirement Traceability Comments
80: 
81: All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.

327: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)

Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand.

331: ```mermaid
332: flowchart TD
333:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
334:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
335:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
336:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
337:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
338:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
339:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
340:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
341:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
342:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
343:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
344:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
345:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
346: ```

391:     K -->|yes| R(["Reviewer id: Cline, Copilot, Claude, Codex, or Grok"])
392:     K -->|no| U2(["Unknown, with the PascalCase form"])
393: ```

395: ### 11.5 TurnSnapshotBuilder (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation`)
396: 
397: Builds the canonical review snapshot of one turn: its turn key, status, `requestClass`, query title and text, interpretation, response, actions, design decisions, files modified, requirements discovered, blockers, tags, context list, and processing dialog, in stored order, with `agentReview` and `hostileReview` left out (R-21), every text through SecretRedactor, serialized as canonical JSON, and hashed through ContentHasher. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand (the snapshot and its hash on each `HvRequestTurn`) and FinalizeHvRequestCommand (V-2 re-hash).
398: 
399: ```mermaid
400: flowchart TD
401:     S(["TurnSnapshotBuilder: turn"]) --> P["Project the listed fields in stored order; omit agentReview and hostileReview"]
402:     P --> R[["SecretRedactor on every text field"]]
403:     R --> J["Serialize as canonical JSON"]
404:     J --> H[["ContentHasher: SHA-256 of the stored normal form"]]
405:     H --> OK(["snapshot JSON and snapshotSha256"])
406: ```
407: 
408: ### 11.6 RequirementReferenceExtractor (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Requirements`)
409: 
410: Extracts the requirement and use-case references of R-23 from the submitted context, in order of first appearance and without duplicates, and resolves each against the workspace's effective requirements (`client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`, the marker's requirements visibility rule) and use cases (by store id or exact title). Returns each reference with `kind`, `id`, `resolved`, and, when resolved, its title and the SHA-256 of its effective record. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand.
411: 
412: ```mermaid
413: flowchart TD
414:     S(["RequirementReferenceExtractor: context text"]) --> X["Scan for FR, TR, TEST ids, acceptance-criterion forms, and use-case references; keep first appearances"]
415:     X --> L{"Any reference found?"}
416:     L -->|no| E(["empty list"])
417:     L -->|yes| R["Resolve each against the effective requirements and the use cases"]
418:     R --> OK(["ordered list: kind, id, resolved, title, sha256"])
419: ```

421: ### 11.7 NotificationOutbox (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation`)
422: 
423: `Append(kind, hvRequestId, reviewerId, runId, payload)` runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite: it increments the workspace's `HvWorkspaceState.NextNotificationSequence`, inserts the `HvNotification` row with that sequence, and registers a post-commit wake-up on `IChangeEventBus` (R-16). Used by every unit whose change a caller observes.
424: 
425: ```mermaid
426: flowchart TD
427:     S(["NotificationOutbox.Append in the caller's transaction"]) --> Q["Read and increment HvWorkspaceState.NextNotificationSequence"]
428:     Q --> I["Insert HvNotification with the sequence, kind, ids, and payload"]
429:     I --> W["Register the post-commit wake-up on IChangeEventBus"]
430:     W --> OK(["appended: sequence; visible only when the caller commits"])
431: ```
432: 
433: ### 11.8 OrderedEventReplay (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Streaming`)
434: 
435: Serves a Server-Sent Events stream from durable ordered rows: parses `Last-Event-ID` (absent means from the beginning of the requested stream, a malformed value is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `Last-Event-ID`), sends every stored event after it in order with its `id:`, then waits on the `IChangeEventBus` wake-up (or a poll interval) and sends new rows; it sends a comment line every 15 seconds while idle so proxies keep the connection, and ends when the caller disconnects or the stream's source reaches a terminal event. Develop's event stream has no replay and no event ids (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/EventStreamController.cs:27-92`); this component adds both without changing that controller. Used by StreamHvRunOutputQuery and StreamHvNotificationsQuery.
436: 
437: ```mermaid
438: flowchart TD
439:     S(["OrderedEventReplay: source, Last-Event-ID"]) --> P{"Last-Event-ID valid or absent?"}
440:     P -->|malformed| E(["400 validation_error, details.field Last-Event-ID"])
441:     P -->|yes| RD["Read stored events after the position, in order"]
442:     RD --> SND["Send each event with its id"]
443:     SND --> T{"Source terminal and all events sent?"}
444:     T -->|yes| END(["stream ended with the terminal event"])
445:     T -->|no| WT["Wait for a wake-up or the poll interval; send a comment every 15 seconds while idle"]
446:     WT --> DC{"Caller disconnected?"}
447:     DC -->|yes| END2(["stream closed"])
448:     DC -->|no| RD
449: ```

The server compares both `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json` `generatedAtUtc` values and the latest `lastModifiedUtc` per platform. If both checks agree, the newer platform is selected. If they disagree and no preference is supplied, import fails. The selected platform folder is authoritative: missing records are deleted, changed records are updated, new records are created, and identical records are ignored.

526: ## Error Handling
527: 
528: Common error codes:
529: 
530: - `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
531: - `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create
532: - `invalid_requirement_id` - ID does not match the expected regex for its type
533: - `mapping_not_found` - mapping between the specified FR and TR does not exist
534: - `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID
535: - `document_generation_error` - failed to render the requested document format
536: - `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document
537: 
538: ## Workflow Recommendations
539: 
540: When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:
541: 
542: 1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
543: 2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
544: 3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
545: 4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
546: 5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`
547: 
548: Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.

542: ### 13.3 Reviewer contract, version 1
543: 
544: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there (R-24), to close that turn through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
545: 
546: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
547: 
548: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
549: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
550: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
551: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN" }] }`: one per linked response with disposition `Pending` (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once).
552: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
553: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
554: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
555: 
556: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
557: 
558: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
559: 
560: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
561: 
562: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
563: 
564: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN, each with its remediation (S-13); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
565: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
566: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.

568: ### 13.5 Streams
569: 
570: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.

530: - `UpdateHvReviewerRequest { enabled, executionStrategy, agentPath, model, effort, maxConcurrentRuns, expectedStateVersion }`: every field but `expectedStateVersion` optional; `model` and `effort` accept an empty string to return to the default.
531: - `StartHvReviewerNonceResult { reviewerId, status, probeRequestedUtc, runId }` (202 Accepted): `status` `Requested` (a new probe is waiting for the worker), `AlreadyRequested`, or `Running` (with the probe's `runId`); the outcome arrives as a `reviewer_online` or `reviewer_offline` notification and on the reviewer.
532: - `SubmitHvRequestRequest { scope: { kind, agent, sessionId, requestId, fromRequestId, toRequestId }, submitter: { kind, agent, sessionId, requestId, operatorName }, context, contextFormat, idempotencyKey }`: `scope.kind` `Turn` needs `requestId`, `Range` needs `fromRequestId` and `toRequestId`, `Session` needs neither (S-03, S-11); `submitter.kind` `Agent` needs the full turn key, `Operator` needs `operatorName` (R-09); `context` is optional, at most 65536 characters; `contextFormat` defaults to `Markdown`.
533: - `HvRequestResult { hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, assignedReviewerId, attemptCount, excludedSubmittingTurn, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, requestClassAtAdmission, hostileStatusAtAdmission, disposition }], requirementRefs: [{ kind, refId, resolved, title }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, disposition, closedReason, notGradedReason, gradeId }], currentRun: { runId, reviewerId, status, attempt, startedUtc, lastHeartbeatUtc, lastOutputUtc, progress: { percentComplete, etaSeconds, etaStatus, reportedUtc }, lastOutput: [string] }, overallVerdict, holisticVerdict, failureCode, createdUtc, startedUtc, completedUtc }`: `lastOutput` holds the last 20 output lines of the current run (S-18, "their last reported output"); `etaStatus` is `Reported` or `Unknown` (R-18); summaries in a page leave `turns`, `requirementRefs`, `responses`, and `lastOutput` null.
534: - `HvRequestQuery { status, agent, sessionId, reviewerId, submitterAgent, limit, offset }` returns `PageResult<HvRequestResult>` (PagedQuery, `PageBounds` `Refuse`, order `CreatedUtc` descending then `HvRequestId`).
535: - `CancelHvRequestResult { hvRequestId, previousStatus, status }`.
536: - `HvNotificationDto { sequence, kind, hvRequestId, reviewerId, runId, payload, createdUtc }`; `HvNotificationQuery { afterSequence, limit }` returns `{ items, lastSequence }`.
537: - `HvIncidentDto { incidentId, reviewerId, runId, hvRequestId, failureCode, dedupeKey, summary, filingStatus, filingAttempts, triageReportId, triageGroupId, createdUtc, filedUtc }`.
538: - `RemoveHvEvidenceRequest { reason, removedBy }` returns `RemoveHvEvidenceResult { hvRequestId, removedKinds, removedChunks, removedUtc }`.
539: - `HvIncidentQuery { reviewerId, filingStatus, limit, offset }`; `HvNotificationPage { items, lastSequence }`; `HvOutputEvent { runId, sequence, lines, closedStatus }` (the item type of the output stream, section 13.5).
540: - Server-side result types that never cross the wire as JSON: `HvEvidenceStream` (the evidence bytes with their content type, file name, SHA-256, and sizes, written to the response body by the controller), and the internal unit results of section 14.4 (`HvRunClaim`, `HvHeartbeatResult`, `HvAppendResult`, `HvCloseResult`, `HvFailResult`, `HvSweepResult`, `HvFinalizeResult`, `HvProvenance`), defined in `src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/`.
541: 
542: ### 13.3 Reviewer contract, version 1
543: 
544: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there (R-24), to close that turn through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
545: 
546: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
547: 
548: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
549: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
550: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
551: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN" }] }`: one per linked response with disposition `Pending` (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once).
552: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
553: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
554: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
555: 
556: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
557: 
558: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
559: 
560: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
561: 
562: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
563: 
564: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN, each with its remediation (S-13); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
565: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
566: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.
567: 
568: ### 13.5 Streams
569: 
570: - Output stream: event `hv_output` with `id` `<runId>:<sequence>` and data `{ runId, sequence, lines: [string] }`, one event per stored chunk; event `hv_run_closed` with data `{ runId, status }` when the run ends; a new attempt starts a new run id in the same stream, so `Last-Event-ID` `<runId>:<sequence>` resumes after that chunk of that run. Per S-18 a caller attaches to "any running hv": the stream serves the request's runs in attempt order.
571: - Notification stream: event `<kind>` with `id` `<sequence>` and data `HvNotificationDto`; `Last-Event-ID` `<sequence>` resumes after it. The stream is workspace-scoped (S-19: notifications of HV completion in the plugins).
572: 
573: ### 13.6 Error codes
574: 
575: New entries of the one `ErrorCodes` table (foundation section 3.5.2), each with its status and retryable flag:
576: 
577: - `audit_unavailable` 503, retryable (AuditLedgerGuard).
578: - `review_hostile_pipeline_only` 403 (A-06).
579: - `turn_immutable` 409 with `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` and `details.hvRequestId` (the code exists in the foundation's typed failures, C9; A-07 adds the reasons).
580: - `hv_no_reviewer_available` 409 with `details.reviewers` (each reviewer's id, enabled flag, readiness, reason, and open incident) (S-16).
581: - `hv_scope_invalid` 400 (`details.field`: an unknown kind, a missing or extra scope field, an unknown session, an endpoint turn not in the session, or a range whose start is after its end).
582: - `hv_scope_too_large` 400 (`details.count`, `details.max`).
583: - `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` 400.
584: - `hv_scope_empty` 400 (a session scope with no turn left after the submitting turn's exclusion).
585: - `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed` 409, each with `details.turns` (and `details.hvRequestIds` for the second and third).
586: - `hv_request_not_cancelable` 409 (`details.status`).
587: - `hv_request_active` 409 (`details.status`: evidence removal of a request that is not `Completed`, `Failed`, or `Canceled`).
588: - `hv_reviewer_disabled` 409 (a NONCE requested for a disabled reviewer).
589: - `hv_result_not_ready` 409 (`details.status`).
590: - `hv_evidence_not_available` 404 (a kind not produced yet) and `hv_evidence_removed` 410.
591: - `conflict` 409: `retryable: false` for an idempotency key reused with other inputs or a reviewer update whose `expectedStateVersion` is stale (`details.field` `expectedStateVersion`), `retryable: true` when SerializableWrite or ReadableKeyAllocator is exhausted.
592: - `not_found` 404 with `details.resource` `reviewer`, `hv_request`, or `run`.
593: - `evidence_corrupt` 500: a GZIP round trip failed inside admission (SubmitHvRequestCommand) and nothing was saved; on runs it is also an internal failure code.
594: - Internal codes, stored on runs and incidents and never returned by a public route: `stale_fence`, `evidence_corrupt`, `reviewer_launch_failed`, `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, `reviewer_output_invalid`, `reviewer_turn_unverified`, `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, `verdict_binding_failed`, `reviewer_not_independent`, `snapshot_changed`, `probe_nonce_mismatch`, `lease_expired`, `attempts_exhausted`, `canceled`, `worker_shutdown`.
595: 
596: ## 14. Units of work (CQRS handlers)
597: 
598: Each unit is one command or query record and its handler, two files in the folders of section 4. WorkspaceResolutionBehavior runs after the dispatch and before every handler (foundation section 3.5.1); each unit lists its 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath` and does not draw it. Every command runs its checks and its save as one SerializableWrite delegate (foundation section 3.5.2) and calls AuditLedgerGuard first inside it (R-19), so each command lists 503 `audit_unavailable` and 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (attempts exhausted, nothing saved) and draws them once as the exits of its SerializableWrite call. Reviewer ids in routes and filters pass through AgentIdentity, so an alias addresses its reviewer.
599: 
600: ### 14.1 Reviewer pool and readiness
601: 
602: #### ListHvReviewersQuery: list the reviewer pool [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003]
603: 
604: - Handler: `ListHvReviewersQuery(string WorkspacePath) : IQuery<IReadOnlyList<HvReviewerDto>>`.
605: - Surfaces: section 13.1. Response 200: the five reviewers in pool order (Cline, Copilot, Claude, Codex, Grok), each with `activeRuns` (its runs in `Claimed` or `Running`).
606: - Errors: 400 `validation_error` (`workspacePath`).
607: 
608: ```mermaid
609: flowchart TD
610:     S(["Handler runs: GET reviewers"]) --> L["Load the workspace's HvReviewer rows in pool order"]
611:     L --> C["Count each reviewer's runs in Claimed or Running"]
612:     C --> R(["200 the five HvReviewerDto"])
613: ```
614: 
615: #### GetHvReviewerQuery: get one reviewer [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003]
616: 
617: - Handler: `GetHvReviewerQuery(string WorkspacePath, string ReviewerId) : IQuery<HvReviewerDto>`.
618: - Response 200 `HvReviewerDto`. Errors: 400 `validation_error` (`workspacePath`); 404 `not_found` (`details.resource` `reviewer`) for an id AgentIdentity does not map to a reviewer.
619: 
620: ```mermaid
621: flowchart TD
622:     S(["Handler runs: GET reviewers/{reviewerId}"]) --> N[["AgentIdentity.Normalize"]]
623:     N -->|Unknown| E(["404 not_found, details.resource reviewer"])
624:     N -->|reviewer id| L["Load the row and count its active runs"]
625:     L --> R(["200 HvReviewerDto"])
626: ```
627: 
628: #### UpdateHvReviewerCommand: manage a reviewer in real time [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001]
629: 
630: - Handler: `UpdateHvReviewerCommand(string WorkspacePath, string ReviewerId, UpdateHvReviewerRequest Request) : ICommand<HvReviewerDto>` (S-02).
631: - Validation before the transaction: `expectedStateVersion` required; `executionStrategy`, when present, a supported strategy name; `maxConcurrentRuns` in 1..8; `model` at most 128 and `effort` at most 32 characters; any violation is 400 `validation_error` naming the field.
632: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; the reviewer row (404 when absent); `StateVersion` equal to `expectedStateVersion`, otherwise 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false` and `details.field` `expectedStateVersion`; apply the fields; when the strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed, set `Readiness` `Unverified` with reason `configuration_changed` and append `reviewer_unverified` (NotificationOutbox); increment `StateVersion`. After the commit the worker is woken, and it NONCEs an enabled `Unverified` reviewer (R-10).
633: - A disabled reviewer stays assigned to the requests it holds until their next claim, which reassigns them (R-07); a run already running continues.
634: - Response 200 `HvReviewerDto`. Errors: 400 `validation_error`; 404 `not_found` (`reviewer`); 409 `conflict` (`retryable: false` stale version, `retryable: true` exhausted); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
635: 
636: ```mermaid
637: flowchart TD
638:     S(["Handler runs: PATCH reviewers/{reviewerId}"]) --> V{"Fields valid and expectedStateVersion present?"}
639:     V -->|no| E1(["400 validation_error, naming the field"])
640:     V -->|yes| N[["AgentIdentity.Normalize"]]
641:     N -->|Unknown| E2(["404 not_found, details.resource reviewer"])
642:     N -->|reviewer id| SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
643:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E3(["503 audit_unavailable"])
644:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E4(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
645:     SW -->|attempt| VER{"StateVersion equals expectedStateVersion?"}
646:     VER -->|no| E5(["409 conflict, retryable false, details.field expectedStateVersion"])
647:     VER -->|yes| AP["Apply the fields"]
648:     AP --> CH{"Strategy, agent path, model, or effort changed?"}
649:     CH -->|yes| UV["Readiness Unverified, reason configuration_changed"]
650:     UV --> NO[["NotificationOutbox: reviewer_unverified"]]
651:     NO --> INC["Increment StateVersion"]
652:     CH -->|no| INC
653:     INC --> R(["200 HvReviewerDto; the worker is woken after the commit"])
654: ```
655: 
656: #### StartHvReviewerNonceCommand: request a NONCE probe [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003]
657: 
658: - Handler: `StartHvReviewerNonceCommand(string WorkspacePath, string ReviewerId) : ICommand<StartHvReviewerNonceResult>` (S-27, R-10). Any caller may request it (no roles, S-29).
659: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; the reviewer row (404); a disabled reviewer is 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`; a probe run of this reviewer in `Claimed` or `Running` returns 202 `Running` with its run id and writes nothing; a `ProbeRequestedUtc` already set returns 202 `AlreadyRequested` and writes nothing; otherwise `ProbeRequestedUtc` is set and the result is 202 `Requested`. After the commit the worker is woken; ClaimHvRunCommand creates the probe run.
660: - Errors: 400 `validation_error` (`workspacePath`); 404 `not_found` (`reviewer`); 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`, `conflict` (`retryable: true`); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
661: 
662: ```mermaid
663: flowchart TD
664:     S(["Handler runs: POST reviewers/{reviewerId}/nonce"]) --> N[["AgentIdentity.Normalize"]]
665:     N -->|Unknown| E1(["404 not_found, details.resource reviewer"])
666:     N -->|reviewer id| SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
667:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E2(["503 audit_unavailable"])
668:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E3(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
669:     SW -->|attempt| EN{"Reviewer enabled?"}
670:     EN -->|no| E4(["409 hv_reviewer_disabled"])

679: ### 14.2 Admission, queries, and cancellation
680: 
681: #### SubmitHvRequestCommand: admit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -007, -011, -013, -018]
682: 
683: - Handler: `SubmitHvRequestCommand(string WorkspacePath, SubmitHvRequestRequest Request) : ICommand<HvRequestResult>`.
684: - Callers: any agent or operator; the plugin verb `workflow.hv.submit` binds the submitting turn automatically (process SubmitHvFromPlugin, section 16.4).
685: - Order of checks:
686:   1. Shape (no store read): the scope fields for its kind (400 `hv_scope_invalid` with `details.field`), the submitter fields for its kind (400 `validation_error` with `details.field` under `submitter`), a nonblank `idempotencyKey` of at most 128 characters, `contextFormat` known and `context` at most 65536 characters (400 `validation_error`).
687:   2. Reads before the transaction (foundation section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): RequirementReferenceExtractor over `context`.
688:   3. SerializableWrite delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; IdempotentCreate on `IdempotencyKey` (policy `Conflict`, fingerprint of the client inputs): the same inputs return 200 with the stored request, other inputs 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`; TurnLocator on the submitting turn for `submitter.kind` `Agent` (`InvalidIdentifier`, `SessionNotFound`, or `TurnNotFound` is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `submitter`); policy HvScopeResolution; policy HvAdmissionEligibility; policy RoundRobinAssignment; then the inserts.
689:   4. Inserts in the delegate: the `hvr-` key (ReadableKeyAllocator); `HvRequest` `Queued` with `AssignedReviewerId` and `AuthorReviewerId`; one `HvRequestTurn` per member, each with its TurnSnapshotBuilder snapshot hash, class, and hostile status at admission (S-09); the requirement references; one `HvRequestResponse` `Pending` per agent response of a member turn whose status is `Submitted`, `Grading`, `Trusted`, or `Stale` and that is not `Pending` in another open request (when Phase C has recorded responses); the `Request` evidence through GzipCodec (section 13.3); policy HvTurnFreeze `Freeze` on every member turn (`HvState` `Pending`, `HvRequestId`); the round-robin cursor advance; NotificationOutbox `hv_queued`.
690:   5. After the commit the worker is woken (S-24, auto-start).
691: - Response 201 `HvRequestResult` with Location `/qbrainai/hostile-validation/requests/{hvRequestId}`; a repeat with the same key and inputs is 200 with the stored request and its current state.
692: - Concurrency: two submissions over overlapping turns are serialized by SerializableWrite; the second sees the first's `Pending` items and is refused with `hv_turns_pending` (I-01; the unique filtered index ends a racing insert, and the retried attempt finds the winner). Two submissions over disjoint turns take consecutive cursor values, so round-robin order holds under concurrency.
693: - Errors, in order: 400 `hv_scope_invalid`, `validation_error` (submitter, key, context, `workspacePath`), `hv_scope_too_large`, `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn`, `hv_scope_empty`; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: false` key reused, `retryable: true` exhausted), `hv_turns_not_terminal`, `hv_turns_pending`, `hv_turns_already_reviewed`, `hv_no_reviewer_available` (with `details.reviewers`); 500 `evidence_corrupt` (the accepted request failed its GZIP round trip; nothing saved); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
694: 
695: ```mermaid
696: flowchart TD
697:     S(["Handler runs: POST requests"]) --> SH{"Scope, submitter, key, and context well formed?"}
698:     SH -->|"scope"| E1(["400 hv_scope_invalid, details.field"])
699:     SH -->|"submitter, key, or context"| E2(["400 validation_error, details.field"])
700:     SH -->|yes| RX[["RequirementReferenceExtractor on the context"]]
701:     RX --> SW[["SerializableWrite with AuditLedgerGuard"]]
702:     SW -->|"audit unavailable"| E3(["503 audit_unavailable"])
703:     SW -->|"attempts exhausted"| E4(["409 conflict, retryable true"])
704:     SW -->|attempt| IC[["IdempotentCreate lookup, policy Conflict"]]
705:     IC -->|"stored, same inputs"| R2(["200 the stored request"])
706:     IC -->|"key reused, other inputs"| E5(["409 conflict, retryable false"])
707:     IC -->|absent| AC[["AdmitRequestChecks"]]
708:     AC -->|refused| E6(["Refusal of AdmitRequestChecks, drawn there"])
709:     AC -->|"members and reviewer"| INS[["InsertAdmittedRequest"]]
710:     INS -->|"key collision: attempt ends"| SW
711:     INS -->|committed| R(["201 HvRequestResult; the worker is woken after the commit"])
712: ```

810: 
811: #### GetHvResultQuery: the standard result document [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-010, -015]
812: 
813: - Handler: `GetHvResultQuery(string WorkspacePath, string HvRequestId) : IQuery<HvResultDocument>` (S-13, section 13.4).
814: - Order: the request (404); `Completed` required, otherwise 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the status; evidence removed is 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it keeps; AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead`; then the document is assembled from the `Result` evidence and the `Request` evidence (GzipCodec) and the finalized run's chunks, streamed in order.
815: - Errors: 400 `validation_error` (`workspacePath`); 404 `not_found` (`hv_request`); 409 `hv_result_not_ready`; 410 `hv_evidence_removed`; 503 `audit_unavailable`.
816: 
817: ```mermaid
818: flowchart TD
819:     S(["Handler runs: GET requests/{hvRequestId}/result"]) --> F{"Request in the workspace?"}
820:     F -->|no| E1(["404 not_found, details.resource hv_request"])
821:     F -->|yes| C{"Status Completed?"}
822:     C -->|no| E2(["409 hv_result_not_ready, details.status"])
823:     C -->|yes| RM{"Evidence removed?"}
824:     RM -->|yes| E3(["410 hv_evidence_removed, hashes and sizes kept"])
825:     RM -->|no| A[["AuditLedgerGuard RecordRead"]]
826:     A -->|"audit unavailable"| E4(["503 audit_unavailable"])
827:     A -->|recorded| D[["GzipCodec Decompress: Result and Request evidence"]]
828:     D --> LG["Stream the finalized run's chunks in order as responseLog"]
829:     LG --> R(["200 HvResultDocument, gzip when the caller accepts it"])
830: ```

832: #### GetHvEvidenceQuery: download evidence [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011, -015]
833: 
834: - Handler: `GetHvEvidenceQuery(string WorkspacePath, string HvRequestId, string Kind, string? RunId, bool Decompressed) : IQuery<HvEvidenceStream>`.
835: - `Kind` `request` (from admission), `response-log` (the finalized run, or `runId` for any run of the request, including a running one, so a caller can fetch output before finalization), or `result` (only when `Completed`). The default answer is `application/gzip`: the stored GZIP member for `request` and `result`, and for `response-log` the run's chunks served as consecutive GZIP members, which is a valid GZIP stream (RFC 1952, section 2.2); with `Decompressed` the bytes are decompressed on the way (`application/x-ndjson` or `application/json`). Nothing uncompressed is stored (R-14). AuditLedgerGuard `RecordRead` runs before the first byte.
836: - Errors: 400 `validation_error` (`workspacePath`, an unknown `kind`); 404 `not_found` (`hv_request`; `run` for a `runId` that does not exist or belongs to another request), `hv_evidence_not_available` (a kind not produced yet); 410 `hv_evidence_removed`; 503 `audit_unavailable`.
837: 
838: ```mermaid

1370: ### 16.1 Process HvWorkerHost: the durable worker [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008, -009]
1371: 
1372: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix. It is the only dispatcher of the internal units (R-29). At start, while `WorkerEnabled`, it requests a NONCE for every enabled `Unverified` reviewer (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand, R-10). Then it loops, woken by an `IChangeEventBus` wake-up or at `PollInterval`: a sweep (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request it lists, FileHvIncidentCommand for every `Pending` incident), then claims until ClaimHvRunCommand returns null, starting one process RunReviewerProcess per claim. 1393: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1394: 
1395: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, or the probe brief with its nonce), asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has three concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) whenever `OutputFlushInterval` passes or `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).

1442: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:

The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. 1445: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1446: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1447: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. 1344: ### Policy HvRetryDecision: requeue, fail, or cancel [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -009]
1345: 
1346: Applied inside the caller's transaction by FailHvRunCommand and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand for a review run's request; it decides the request's next state and writes it, so a request ends the same way whether its attempt failed or its worker died. A `CancelRequested` request becomes `Canceled`; otherwise, with the counted attempts (the request's runs except those that ended `worker_shutdown`, which a graceful restart causes and no reviewer does) below `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` the request returns to `Queued` (its assignee re-evaluated at the next claim, R-07); otherwise it becomes `Failed` with `attempts_exhausted`. A canceled or failed request gets `CompletedUtc`, releases its turns (HvTurnFreeze `Release`), closes its `Pending` responses with `request_ended`, and appends `hv_canceled` or `hv_failed` (NotificationOutbox).
1347: 
1348: ```mermaid
1349: flowchart TD
1350:     S(["HvRetryDecision: request, in the caller's transaction"]) --> C{"CancelRequested?"}
1351:     C -->|yes| CN["Request Canceled with CompletedUtc; Pending responses Closed request_ended"]
1352:     CN --> RL1[["Policy HvTurnFreeze Release"]]
1353:     RL1 --> N1[["NotificationOutbox: hv_canceled"]]
1354:     N1 --> R1(["cancel: request Canceled"])
1355:     C -->|no| A{"Counted attempts, worker_shutdown excluded, below MaxAttemptsPerRequest?"}
1356:     A -->|yes| QD["Request Queued; assignee re-evaluated at the next claim"]
1357:     QD --> R2(["requeue: request Queued"])
1358:     A -->|no| FL["Request Failed attempts_exhausted with CompletedUtc; Pending responses Closed request_ended"]
1359:     FL --> RL2[["Policy HvTurnFreeze Release"]]
1360:     RL2 --> N2[["NotificationOutbox: hv_failed"]]
1361:     N2 --> R3(["fail: request Failed"])
1362: ```

1364: ### Reused policy HvVerdictMapping
1365: 
1366: Foundation section 5.3, unchanged in its rule; its only caller is now RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand dispatched by FinalizeHvRequestCommand with origin `HvFinalization` (A-06).
1367: 
1368: ## 16. Processes
1369: 
1370: ### 16.1 Process HvWorkerHost: the durable worker [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008, -009]
1371: 
1372: A hosted `BackgroundService` per workspace application (`src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/Execution/HvWorkerHost.cs`), with a worker id of the host name, process id, and a random suffix. It is the only dispatcher of the internal units (R-29). At start, while `WorkerEnabled`, it requests a NONCE for every enabled `Unverified` reviewer (StartHvReviewerNonceCommand, R-10). Then it loops, woken by an `IChangeEventBus` wake-up or at `PollInterval`: a sweep (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request it lists, FileHvIncidentCommand for every `Pending` incident), then claims until ClaimHvRunCommand returns null, starting one process RunReviewerProcess per claim. On a graceful shutdown it stops claiming and ends each of its running runs with FailHvRunCommand code `worker_shutdown`, which files no incident, marks no reviewer offline, and does not count as an attempt (policy HvRetryDecision); after a crash the leases expire instead (W-03). A 503 `audit_unavailable` from any unit stops the loop iteration and the next iteration starts from the sweep (W-12).
1373: 
1374: ```mermaid
1375: flowchart TD
1376:     S(["HvWorkerHost starts"]) --> EN{"WorkerEnabled?"}
1377:     EN -->|no| IDLE(["idle: no claims"])
1378:     EN -->|yes| NV[["StartHvReviewerNonceCommand for each enabled Unverified reviewer"]]
1379:     NV --> W["Wait for a wake-up or PollInterval"]
1380:     W --> SD{"Shutting down?"}
1381:     SD -->|yes| FS[["FailHvRunCommand worker_shutdown for each own running run"]]
1382:     FS --> END(["stopped"])
1383:     SD -->|no| SW[["ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand"]]
1384:     SW -->|audit_unavailable| W
1385:     SW -->|"sweep result"| FZ[["FinalizeHvRequestCommand for each Finalizing request"]]
1386:     FZ --> FI[["FileHvIncidentCommand for each Pending incident"]]
1387:     FI --> CL[["ClaimHvRunCommand"]]
1388:     CL -->|"null, audit_unavailable, or conflict"| W
1389:     CL -->|claim| RP[["Process RunReviewerProcess, started for this claim"]]
1390:     RP --> CL
1391: ```
1392: 
1393: ### 16.2 Process RunReviewerProcess: one attempt, live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008, -016]
1394: 
1395: Runs one claimed run. It builds the brief (section 13.3: the accepted request read from the `Request` evidence inside the run envelope, or the probe brief with its nonce), asks the reviewer's adapter for the launch (section 16.3), starts the process with the workspace as its working directory and its plugin as a host session of its own (R-24), and appends the `hv_brief` record as sequence 1. While the process runs it has three concurrent duties and no time limit (R-11, P-02): every line the adapter delivers goes into a buffer that is appended (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) whenever `OutputFlushInterval` passes or `OutputFlushBytes` accumulate (R-12); a heartbeat every `HeartbeatInterval` (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand) renews the lease and reads cancellation; and the process exit is awaited. `stale_fence` from any unit kills the process and ends the attempt without another write (W-03); `audit_unavailable` kills the process and ends the attempt (W-12); a retryable `conflict` repeats the same unit call with the same sequence. Every append carries the records the adapter's extraction completed with that batch. On exit the remaining buffer is appended, the adapter's provenance lines are appended (section 16.3), and the run is closed (exit code 0, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand for a review; exit code 0 is not evidence of a review, R-11) or failed (FailHvRunCommand with `reviewer_exited_nonzero`, or `reviewer_launch_failed` when the process never started). A cancellation read at a heartbeat kills the process and fails the run with `canceled`, which policy HvRetryDecision turns into the request's `Canceled` (R-28). Killing the process, here and in the diagrams, ends the reviewer's whole process tree, descendants included, also when the root process has already exited; and when the root exits while a descendant still holds its output pipes, the worker ends that descendant before it reads the output to its end. Without that, a descendant that outlives the reviewer would hold the run open forever, because no time limit ends a run (P-02); P14 is the same defect class in the plugin core (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011).
1396: 
1397: ```mermaid
1398: flowchart TD
1399:     S(["RunReviewerProcess: claim"]) --> B["Build the brief: accepted request in the run envelope, or the probe brief"]
1400:     B --> L[["Reviewer adapter BuildLaunch"]]
1401:     L --> ST{"Process started?"}
1402:     ST -->|no| FL[["FailHvRunCommand reviewer_launch_failed"]]
1403:     FL --> END1(["attempt ended"])
1404:     ST -->|yes| A1[["AppendHvRunOutputCommand: sequence 1, the hv_brief record"]]
1405:     A1 --> RUN[["StreamReviewerOutput: lines, flushes, heartbeats, until exit, stale fence, audit failure, or cancel"]]
1406:     RUN -->|"stale_fence or audit_unavailable"| K1["Kill the process"]
1407:     K1 --> END2(["attempt ended, no further write"])
1408:     RUN -->|"cancel requested"| K2["Kill the process"]
1409:     K2 --> FC[["FailHvRunCommand canceled"]]
1410:     FC --> END3(["attempt ended: request Canceled"])
1411:     RUN -->|"exited"| FLS[["AppendHvRunOutputCommand: remaining lines, then the adapter's hv_provenance lines"]]
1412:     FLS --> EX{"Exit code 0?"}
1413:     EX -->|no| FN[["FailHvRunCommand reviewer_exited_nonzero"]]
1414:     FN --> END4(["attempt ended"])
1415:     EX -->|yes| CO[["CloseHvRunOutputCommand"]]
1416:     CO -->|"Review: Finalizing"| FZ[["FinalizeHvRequestCommand"]]
1417:     FZ --> END5(["attempt ended: request Completed, Queued, or Failed"])
1418:     CO -->|"Probe: passed or failed"| END6(["attempt ended: reviewer Online or Offline"])
1419: ```

1422:

1426:     E -->|"line from the adapter"| BUF["Add the JSONL line to the buffer"]
1427:     BUF --> FT{"Flush interval passed or flush bytes reached?"}
1428:     FT -->|no| E
1429:     FT -->|yes| AP[["AppendHvRunOutputCommand: the buffer as the next sequence"]]
1430:     AP -->|appended| E
1431:     AP -->|"retryable conflict"| AP
1432:     AP -->|"stale_fence or audit_unavailable"| X1(["stop: stale fence or audit failure"])
1433:     E -->|"heartbeat timer"| HB[["RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand"]]
1434:     HB -->|"renewed, no cancel"| E
1435:     HB -->|"cancelRequested"| X2(["stop: cancel requested"])
1436:     HB -->|"stale_fence or audit_unavailable"| X1
1437:     E -->|"process exited"| X3(["stop: exited, with the exit code"])
1438: ```
1439: 
1440: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1441: 
1442: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1443: 
1444: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`). The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1445: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1446: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1447: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1448: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1449: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

1495: Participants: `Caller` is any surface's caller (a plugin through the REPL, the REPL, Director, an MCP client, or a REST client); `API` is the controller or MCP tool, which dispatches through `IDispatcher`; `Pipe` is WorkspaceResolutionBehavior; `H` is the unit's handler; `DB` is the relational store; `W` is process HvWorkerHost with RunReviewerProcess; `AD` is the reviewer adapter and its process; `TG` is `ITriageService`. Every sequence that dispatches draws the workspace refusal after the dispatch (foundation section 3, "Errors"); a body that does not bind keeps the existing validation problem. Shared components appear as one message.

1715: ### 17.7 A review attempt, from claim to finalization
1716: 
1717: ```mermaid
1718: sequenceDiagram
1719:     participant W
1720:     participant H
1721:     participant DB
1722:     participant AD
1723:     W->>H: ClaimHvRunCommand
1724:     H->>DB: SerializableWrite: oldest Queued request, eligible reviewer with capacity, FencedLease Claim
1725:     alt nothing claimable
1726:         H-->>W: null
1727:     else claimed
1728:         DB-->>H: run Claimed, request Running, hv_started
1729:         H-->>W: claim with fence token
1730:         W->>AD: BuildLaunch and start the process
1731:         alt launch failed
1732:             W->>H: FailHvRunCommand reviewer_launch_failed
1733:             Note over W,H: ref the execution failure sequence, 17.8
1734:         else started
1735:             W->>H: AppendHvRunOutputCommand sequence 1, the hv_brief record
1736:             Note over W,AD: ref StreamOneAttempt (below)
1737:             alt stale fence or audit unavailable during the run
1738:                 W->>AD: kill the process
1739:                 Note over W: attempt ends without another write, the lease expires later, 17.9
1740:             else cancel requested
1741:                 W->>AD: kill the process
1742:                 W->>H: FailHvRunCommand canceled
1743:             else exited with a nonzero code
1744:                 W->>H: FailHvRunCommand reviewer_exited_nonzero
1745:             else exited with code 0
1746:                 W->>H: AppendHvRunOutputCommand, the remaining lines and the hv_provenance lines
1747:                 W->>H: CloseHvRunOutputCommand with the chunk count
1748:                 H-->>W: request Finalizing
1749:                 Note over W,H: ref FinalizeOneRequest (below)
1750:             end
1751:         end
1752:     end
1753: ```

1755: #### Nested sequence: StreamOneAttempt (the live part of the review attempt)
1756: 
1757: ```mermaid
1758: sequenceDiagram
1759:     participant W
1760:     participant H
1761:     participant DB
1762:     participant AD
1763:     loop until the process exits, a stale fence, an audit failure, or a cancel
1764:         alt a line arrives
1765:             AD-->>W: output line, at once
1766:             W->>W: add to the buffer
1767:             opt flush interval passed or flush bytes reached
1768:                 W->>H: AppendHvRunOutputCommand with the next sequence
1769:                 alt appended
1770:                     H->>DB: chunk stored, manifest and progress updated
1771:                     H-->>W: appended, streams woken
1772:                 else retryable conflict
1773:                     H-->>W: 409 conflict, retryable true
1774:                     W->>H: the same append again
1775:                 else stale fence or audit unavailable
1776:                     H-->>W: stale_fence or 503 audit_unavailable
1777:                 end
1778:             end
1779:         else the heartbeat timer fires
1780:             W->>H: RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand
1781:             alt renewed
1782:                 H-->>W: lease extended, cancelRequested false
1783:             else cancel requested
1784:                 H-->>W: cancelRequested true
1785:             else stale fence or audit unavailable
1786:                 H-->>W: stale_fence or 503 audit_unavailable
1787:             end
1788:         end
1789:     end
1790: ```

1792: #### Nested sequence: FinalizeOneRequest (FinalizeHvRequestCommand after a closed attempt)
1793: 
1794: ```mermaid
1795: sequenceDiagram
1796:     participant W
1797:     participant H
1798:     participant DB
1799:     W->>H: FinalizeHvRequestCommand
1800:     alt already Completed
1801:         H-->>W: already_completed, nothing written
1802:     else not Finalizing
1803:         H-->>W: not_finalizable, nothing written
1804:     else Finalizing
1805:         H->>DB: read the run and its chunks, no transaction
1806:         H->>H: policy HvFinalVerification V-1 to V-8

1819:             else committed

1823:         end

2049: ## 18. Use cases
2050: 
2051: The foundation's notation (foundation section 7): actors are stadium shapes on the left, the use case is the central oval, included and extending behaviors are ovals linked `include` or `extend`. Labels `UC-HV-01` to `UC-HV-12` are document labels; the use-case store keys a use case by a numeric surrogate and its title (`src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/UseCaseEntity.cs:12-13`), so H0 creates each under its section title and records the store id beside the label (section 20). Actor names describe participants, not access roles (S-29). One alternate applies to every use case and is not repeated: an unresolved workspace is refused with 400 `validation_error`, `details.field` `workspacePath`. A flow names in parentheses the unit, policy, process, or component that performs a step.

2095: ### 18.2 UC-HV-01 Manage the reviewer pool [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001]
2096: 
2097: Actors: Operator (through Director or the REPL), server. Trigger: the operator lists, inspects, enables, disables, or retunes a reviewer. Preconditions: the server started with the five reviewers configured and seeded (section 10). Main flow: the operator lists the pool (ListHvReviewersQuery), reads one reviewer (GetHvReviewerQuery), and changes its enabled flag, strategy, agent path, model, effort, or concurrency with the state version it read (UpdateHvReviewerCommand); a change to the strategy, agent path, model, or effort makes the reviewer `Unverified`, and the worker NONCEs it (UC-HV-02). 2126: ### 18.4 UC-HV-03 Submit an HV request [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-002, -004, -005, -006, -013, -018]
2127: 
2128: Actors: model (through its plugin) or operator (through Director), any client, server. Trigger: a caller wants a turn, an inclusive range of turns, or a whole session reviewed (S-03, S-11). Preconditions: the turns to review are terminal; for an agent caller, its own turn is bound by the plugin (BindVerbToTurn). Main flow: the caller submits the scope, optional context in Markdown or YAML, and an idempotency key (SubmitHvRequestCommand); the server resolves the requirement references of the context (RequirementReferenceExtractor), resolves the members (HvScopeResolution: the session's turns at admission time for a session scope, without the submitting turn), checks that every member is terminal, not under review, and never reviewed (HvAdmissionEligibility), picks the next eligible reviewer round-robin, never the submitter, the author of the reviewed session, or an alias of either (RoundRobinAssignment, HvReviewerEligibility), snapshots every member without its review records (TurnSnapshotBuilder), stores the complete accepted request compressed (GzipCodec), freezes the members (HvTurnFreeze), announces `hv_queued`, and wakes the worker (auto-start, S-24). Alternates: the same key and inputs return the stored request; the key with other inputs is a conflict; a malformed scope, a scope over the limit, a scope naming the submitting turn, or an empty session scope is refused (400); turns that are not terminal, under review, or already reviewed are refused with every affected turn listed (409); no reviewer is eligible and the request is refused with every reviewer's status, and the plugin adds the reviewers' open incidents and the NONCE remedy (409, S-16); a turn whose class is `Chore` and whose hostile review is `Unnecessary` is admitted and graded like any other (S-09); a turn has no self-review, or any self-review grade or status, and admission is the same (S-28); the audit ledger is unavailable and nothing is written (503, S-29). Postconditions: one `Queued` request with its members frozen `Pending`, its accepted request stored, and its reviewer assigned. Invariants: I-01, I-07, I-08, I-10.

2147: ### 18.5 UC-HV-04 Run a review live [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007, -008]
2148: 
2149: Actors: HV worker, reviewer agent, server. Trigger: a `Queued` request whose reviewer is eligible and has capacity. Preconditions: UC-HV-03 completed. Main flow: the worker claims the request with a lease and a fence (ClaimHvRunCommand); it launches the reviewer with the brief (RunReviewerProcess) and records the brief as the log's first record; every line the reviewer writes is appended within the flush interval (AppendHvRunOutputCommand) and is visible on the output stream while the reviewer runs (S-22); progress records set the request's progress and ETA (R-18); heartbeats renew the lease (RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand); the reviewer reviews each turn and the whole set, logs its own `Chore` turn holding its result, and emits its verdict record last; on exit with code 0 the worker appends the provenance and closes the output (CloseHvRunOutputCommand), and the request becomes `Finalizing`. Alternates: the assignee is no longer eligible and the claim reassigns round-robin; a cancel arrives and the worker stops the reviewer (UC-HV-08); the reviewer fails to start or exits nonzero (UC-HV-09); the worker loses its lease and its writes are refused as stale, so it stops (UC-HV-09); no reviewer is eligible and the request waits `Queued` with an unknown ETA; the reviewer runs for any length of time without a timeout (P-02). Postconditions: the attempt's complete log is stored, compressed, contiguous, and hashed. Invariants: I-05, I-06.
