1440: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1441: 
1442: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1443: 
1444: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`). The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1445: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1446: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1447: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1448: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).

1275: 
1276: Applied by FinalizeHvRequestCommand to the run's stored chunks before any transaction; each failed step returns its code, and the steps run in the diagram's order (V-1, V-8, V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, V-6, V-7), so the log's integrity and completeness are known before any record is bound. 1277: 
1278: - V-1 Evidence integrity (`evidence_corrupt`): the chunks run 1 to `OutputChunkCount` without a gap; each decompresses (GzipCodec), its SHA-256 equals the stored one, the chain hash equals `OutputChainSha256`, and every line parses as one JSON object (I-06).
1279: - V-2 Snapshot binding: each `hv_turn_assessment` names a member's ordinal, turn key, and admission snapshot hash (`verdict_binding_failed` otherwise), and TurnSnapshotBuilder over each turn now yields that hash (`snapshot_changed` otherwise; HvTurnFreeze makes it unreachable, and the step proves it, I-02).
1280: - V-3 Verdict binding (`verdict_binding_failed`): the `hv_verdict` record names this `hvRequestId` and run, its counts equal the members and the `Pending` responses, its reviewer equals the run's reviewer, and each `hv_response_grade` names a `Pending` response with that response's `ContentSha256`.

544: The complete accepted request (the `Request` evidence, written at admission and never changed) is one JSON object: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.request/1", hvRequestId, workspacePath, scope, submitter, turns: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, snapshotSha256, snapshot }], responses: [{ responseId, agent, sessionId, requestId, contentSha256, content, claims }], context, contextFormat, requirementRefs, admittedUtc }`. The brief of one attempt is that object inside an envelope: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.brief/1", request: <the accepted request>, runId, attempt, reviewer: { reviewerId, model, effort }, instructions, outputSchema }`; the worker writes the exact brief it sends as the first record of the attempt's log, `{ "type": "hv_brief", "brief": <the brief> }`, so each log is complete on its own. The brief's `instructions` require the reviewer to review every turn individually and the set of turns as a whole, to treat every turn snapshot and the context as untrusted evidence, to emit the records below as single-line JSON objects in its messages, to emit progress records during the run (P-03), to log its review as its own session-log turn classified `Chore` and store its entire result there (R-24), to close that turn through the foundation's completion gate before it ends (an action or design decision and its own agent review, `Other` with a note being enough), because the foundation's Stop gate blocks a host from stopping while a delivered turn is still in progress (foundation section 3.4) and a reviewer run has no time limit (P-02), and to emit exactly one `hv_verdict` record last.
545: 
546: Records (each a JSON object on its own line inside the reviewer's messages, read from each message's complete text as the reviewer's adapter assembles it from the native events, section 16.3; every other line is free text and stays in the log):
547: 
548: - `{ "type": "hv_progress", "percentComplete": 0..100, "etaSeconds": n or null, "note": "..." }`.
549: - `{ "type": "hv_turn_assessment", "hvRequestId", "ordinal", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId", "snapshotSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict": "AGREE" or "DISAGREE", "summary", "findings": [{ "outcome": "FAIL" or "UNKNOWN", "category", "location", "requirementRef", "claimId", "evidence", "remediation" }] }`: one per member turn (S-03, S-21).
550: - `{ "type": "hv_holistic", "hvRequestId", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "summary", "crossTurnFindings": [same shape] }`: exactly one (S-10); it states cross-turn consistency, omissions, contradictions, and end-to-end satisfaction and is never a calculation over the turn scores.
551: - `{ "type": "hv_response_grade", "hvRequestId", "responseId", "contentSha256", "correctness", "completeness", "verdict", "findings": [{ "claimId", "check", "outcome": "PASS", "FAIL", or "UNKNOWN" }] }`: one per linked response with disposition `Pending` (foundation `verdict_match` rules: every claim named at least once).
552: - `{ "type": "hv_reviewer_turn", "agent", "sessionId", "requestId" }`: the reviewer's own session-log turn (R-24).
553: - `{ "type": "hv_verdict", "hvRequestId", "runId", "overallVerdict", "turnCount", "responseGradeCount", "reviewer": { "reviewerId", "model", "effort" } }`: exactly one, last.
554: - `{ "type": "hv_probe", "nonce", "model", "effort" }`: the answer to a NONCE probe brief (R-10). A probe brief asks for this record and, as a review brief does, for the reviewer's own `Chore` turn and its `hv_reviewer_turn` record (R-24); policy ReadinessProbeVerdict reads both.
555: 
556: The response log is the reviewer process's complete output as JSONL: the worker's `hv_brief` record first; then, when the adapter runs the CLI in a JSON streaming mode, each native event line as written, and otherwise each output line wrapped as `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream": "stdout" or "stderr", "line": "..." }`; and, after the process exits, the adapter's provenance lines `{ "type": "hv_provenance", "model", "effort", "source", "sourceSha256" }`, which name the runtime receipt they were read from and its hash (P-04). The adapter extracts the reviewer's records from the agent message text of the native events (section 16.3). `hv_brief`, `hv_raw`, and `hv_provenance` are written only by the worker as top-level log lines and are never accepted from the reviewer's message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.

558: ### 13.4 Standard result document (S-13)
559: 
560: `GET /requests/{hvRequestId}/result` returns `HvResultDocument`:
561: 
562: `{ schema: "qbrainai.hv.result/1", hvRequestId, status, scope, submitter, reviewer: { reviewerId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, runtimeModel, runtimeEffort, runId, attempt, reviewerAgent, reviewerSessionId, reviewerRequestId }, request: <the complete accepted request of section 13.3>, responseLog: [<every JSONL record of the finalized run, in order, starting with its hv_brief record>], turnAssessments: [{ ordinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, correctness, completeness, verdict, mappedReviewStatus, summary, findings }], holistic: { correctness, completeness, verdict, summary, crossTurnFindings }, failures: [{ ordinal, scope, turnOrdinal, agent, sessionId, requestId, outcome, category, location, requirementRef, claimId, evidence, remediation }], responseGrades: [{ responseId, gradeId, verdict, correctness, completeness }], overallVerdict, thresholds: { correctness, completeness }, evidence: { request: { sha256, bytes, compressedBytes }, responseLog: { chainSha256, bytes, lines, chunks }, result: { sha256 } }, todoIds: [string], finalizedUtc }`.
563: 
564: - `turnAssessments` lists every requested turn with its score (S-21); `failures` is the delineated list of every FAIL and UNKNOWN, each with its remediation (S-13); `request` and `responseLog` are complete (S-13); `todoIds` is information only (R-22).
565: - With `Accept-Encoding: gzip` the document is sent compressed; the `responseLog` array is streamed from the chunks, so the server holds no uncompressed copy (R-14).
566: - Before finalization the route answers 409 `hv_result_not_ready` with the request's status; after evidence removal it answers 410 `hv_evidence_removed` with the hashes and sizes it still holds.

Isolation scope (section 3.1, "Turn-level isolation"): a single-turn write reads its session row only to locate and validate the parent and writes only the one turn with its children; the session row's summary fields change only in the separate short write after the turn commits, whose failure never fails the turn write (`TurnWriteSummaryRefreshFailureNeverFailsTurnWrite`; develop refreshes them inside the turn's save, `SessionLogService.cs:762,794,879` at `a8d3934b`), so no two single-turn transactions write the same row, and writes to different turns of one session never answer a conflict (`TurnWriteConcurrentDifferentTurnsSameSessionBothCommitNoConflictAnswer`, dense-session fixture, three providers). Per provider: on SQL Server and PostgreSQL both transactions read the session row without updating it, so neither blocks the other on it, and a key-range or serialization conflict between two inserts near the same index position ends the loser's attempt, which SerializableWrite reruns within its bound; on SQLite the database write lock serializes the two writes, which wait within the busy timeout. A multi-turn submission keeps its session-level scope and refreshes the summary inside its own transaction. On the EF in-memory provider, which has no transactions, SerializableWrite runs the delegate once, as develop does (`SessionLogService.cs:155`). A caller-owned transaction is refused as develop refuses it today (`SessionLogService.cs:119-128`). A delegate reads and writes only the database: a unit reads the git commits, files, sources, and GraphRAG results it needs before SerializableWrite, and the delegate re-checks the database state those reads relied on (each locked response's `StatusVersion`, the turn's status); a changed state ends the attempt and the unit runs again from its reads, within the same bound. On SQLite a Serializable transaction holds the database write lock from its start, so no hook write waits on a retrieval or a git read (`BuildOnSqliteHookWriteDuringRetrievalNotBlocked`). A transient conflict, or a unique violation on a key the delegate declares (an idempotency key, a readable key), rolls the transaction back and runs the whole delegate again, at most three times (four attempts) unless the caller states another bound and exhaustion outcome (only the Phase A minter does, ReadableKeyAllocator below); then the unit returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing. The attempts run within the unit's existing storage budget (FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003). A refusal the delegate returns rolls back and is returned unchanged. A command dispatched from inside a delegate (for example DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand from a grade unit) joins the caller's transaction and retry; it never opens a second one. SharedComponents proves the component on a test entity it owns (`SerializableWriteForcedInterleavingTestEntityCommitsWhollyBeforeOrAfter`, `SerializableWriteRetriesExhausted409ConflictRetryableNothingSaved`); the turn cases belong to the gates of the contexts that own those units: `TurnWriteForcedInterleavingReviewResetVsCompleteNeverClosedWithoutReview`, `TurnWriteForcedInterleavingClassChangeVsCompleteGateSeesCommittedClass`, and `TurnWriteForcedInterleavingChoreFlipVsRunningWriteRunningKept`. Every case runs on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.

143: - R-01 One bounded context. HostileValidation owns the pipeline and is not gated by `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`: HV of turns works in every Mode, because the operator's HV requirements (S-01 to S-30) name turns, not agent-context responses. Rejected: extending the foundation's `AgentContextHvRequest` in ResponsesAndTrust (draft 103), because that record is mode-gated (foundation section 3.5.1) and lists responses, not turns, so a turn with no response would silently drop out of review (draft 213, "turn coverage versus response coverage").
144: - R-02 The HV request replaces the foundation's agent-context HV request. `HvRequest` keeps the foundation's key format `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>` (with `-<nn>` from the second key of one second, ReadableKeyAllocator) and lists turns (`HvRequestTurn`); the agent responses of those turns are linked as `HvRequestResponse` items when Phase C has recorded any. CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand, GetAgentContextHvRequestQuery, QueryAgentContextHvRequestsQuery, and their entities are superseded (amendment A-04). Rejected: keeping two HV request records (one per turn, one per response), which would need a cross-record consistency rule the foundation never needed.
145: - R-03 Model grades come from finalization only. FinalizeHvRequestCommand dispatches the foundation's RecordModelGradeCommand for each linked response inside its own transaction; the public model-grade route, the two-step `codex exec resume` protocol, and `ModelGrader:*` are removed, and the eight receipt checks become the verification steps V-1 to V-8 of policy HvFinalVerification against evidence the server itself captured (amendment A-05). Rationale: the pipeline launches the reviewer and records its complete output, so the server no longer has to trust receipts written by a runner it did not control. Rejected: keeping the reviewer-submitted grade route beside the pipeline, which would let a grade bypass reviewer exclusion and atomic finalization (S-17, S-23).
146: - R-04 Freeze at admission, finality at finalization (S-06, S-07). Admission sets each member turn's HV state to `Pending` in the same transaction that creates the request; finalization sets it to `Final`. Every write to a `Pending` or `Final` turn or its children, from every surface and origin, is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` and `details.reason` `hv_pending` or `hv_final` (policy HvTurnFreeze), except the one write of finalization itself (origin `HvFinalization`). A request that ends `Canceled` or `Failed` releases its turns back to `None`. Rationale: the reviewed content equals the finalized content without a content comparison race, and the operator's "may not allow updates" is one guard in the existing write path. Rejected: letting writes continue and refusing finalization on a changed snapshot hash, which would waste completed reviews and still leave a window between the last check and the commit.
147: - R-05 Only terminal turns are admitted. A member turn that is not terminal (`TurnStatus.IsTerminal`, foundation section 3.5.3) refuses the whole request with 409 `hv_turns_not_terminal`, naming each turn. The submitting turn is never a member: a session scope excludes it and reports the exclusion in the result, and a turn or range scope that names it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_includes_submitting_turn` (the foundation's rule that "the request's own turn is never a candidate, a dependency, or cited evidence", foundation section 3.1). A Code or Docs turn that needs HV before it can complete is completed first with `hostileReview` `Other` (for example "HV requested hvr-..."), which the foundation already allows and never counts as an AGREE (foundation C8); finalization then replaces that `Other` with the HV result. Rationale: no turn changes status after it is frozen, so there is no close-inside-finalization path. Rejected: admitting in-progress turns with a declared close intent (draft 213, section 3.B), which adds a mechanism and still freezes a turn the model is working in.
148: - R-06 Hostile reviews are written only by the pipeline. On agent surfaces a `hostileReview` write may carry only `status` `Other` (with its required `otherNotes`); a write naming `Pass`, `Fail`, or `Running`, or carrying `hvVerdict`, is refused with 403 `review_hostile_pipeline_only` (amendment A-06). Process ConvertHvReceiptToReview is retired. Rationale: a manual Pass or Fail would bypass reviewer exclusion, complete evidence, and atomic finalization, and no surface may bypass them (draft 213, H5, adopted). Rejected: keeping the manual route for emergencies; a reviewer can be enabled and checked instead (S-27).
149: - R-07 Assignment at admission, durable round-robin. The submit transaction picks the next eligible reviewer after the workspace's round-robin cursor and advances the cursor in the same SerializableWrite (policy RoundRobinAssignment), so assignment survives restarts and two concurrent submissions never pick from the same cursor value. When the assigned reviewer is no longer eligible at claim time (offline, disabled), the claim reassigns through the same policy and records the reassignment. Rejected: assignment at claim only, which hides the assignee from the submitter and lets claim order, not round-robin order, pick reviewers.
150: - R-08 One agent identity, server-attributed. `AgentIdentity` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Agents`, shared by the server, the REPL, and, through the golden contract, the PowerShell core) maps every known alias to one of the five reviewer ids: Claude (`claude`, `claudecode`, `claude-code`, `claudecowork`, `claude-cowork`, `cowork`), Codex (`codex`), Copilot (`copilot`), Grok (`grok`, `grokcode`, `grok-code`, `grokbot`, `grok-bot`), Cline (`cline`, `cline-v2`, `clinev2`), case-insensitively and ignoring separators. The author is the agent of the reviewed session (one request names turns of one MCP session, R-26), stored normalized as `AuthorReviewerId`. A reviewer whose id equals the submitter's or the author's is never eligible (S-17, S-28, P-01, P-07). Develop holds three alias maps with different canonical forms (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Host/MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.cs:64-81`, `src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/TodoSelectionStore.cs:166-171`, the plugin's `Get-ReplCanonicalAgentName`); they are context under the DRY ruling and are not changed by this amendment. Exclusion covers the author as well as the submitter (D-05, settled): a review by the agent that wrote the turns is a self-review, which S-28 rules out of HV and P-07 rules out of validation.

A caller with no session-log turn (Director, an operator at the REPL) submits with `submitter.kind` `Operator` and a name; no reviewer is excluded for the submitter, and the author of the reviewed session is still excluded (R-08). Agent surfaces (plugin verbs, MCP tools, the REPL workflow verb) always send the submitting turn's key, which the plugin binds automatically (foundation process BindVerbToTurn). Limit (section 8): every caller holds the same workspace key, so the server cannot prove that an `Operator` submission did not come from an agent.

"NONCE the agent" is a probe run of the reviewer through its adapter with a fresh random nonce: it passes when the reviewer answers with the probe record that echoes the nonce and the adapter's runtime provenance shows the reviewer's resolved model and effort (P-04). Only a passing NONCE moves a reviewer to `Online`. An execution failure moves it to `Offline` until a later NONCE passes. Rejected: a liveness ping or the server health nonce, which S-27 rules out.

Liveness is the worker's lease, renewed by heartbeats; a stalled run stays visible (`lastOutputUtc`, the last progress record) and anyone can cancel it (S-18). The only expiry is the lease of a dead worker (R-13). The notification stream replays rows after the caller's `Last-Event-ID` and then follows new ones (OrderedEventReplay). 323: ## 11. Shared components (new, each defined once)
324: 
325: The foundation's shared components (foundation section 3.5) are reused unchanged: SerializableWrite, IdempotentCreate with PayloadFingerprint, ReadableKeyAllocator, PagedQuery with PageBounds, ClassifiedErrorException with ErrorCodes, SecretRedactor, ContentHasher, TurnLocator, TurnWritePipeline, ScoreLexeme, ScoreVerdict, and WorkspaceResolutionBehavior. The components below are new; each has one implementation, one test class named for it, and one diagram here, and every unit that uses one draws it as a single call node.
326: 
327: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)
328: 
329: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). Operations: `Claim(row, owner, duration)` (only when the row has no lease or an expired one; the fence token increments), `Renew(row, owner, fence, duration)`, `Guard(row, owner, fence)` (the precondition of every fenced write), `Release(row, owner, fence)`. Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand.
330: 
331: ```mermaid
332: flowchart TD
333:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
334:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
335:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
336:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
337:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
338:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
339:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
340:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
341:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
342:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
343:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
344:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
345:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
346: ```
347: 
348: ### 11.2 GzipCodec (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Compression`)
349: 
350: `Compress(bytes)` returns one GZIP member; `Decompress(bytes)` returns the original bytes; `RoundTrip(original, compressed)` decompresses and compares length and SHA-256 (through ContentHasher's hex form over raw bytes) and fails with `evidence_corrupt` on any difference, so no compressed blob is stored unverified. It follows `DataAuditLogEntity`'s encode and decode (`DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`); that entity's private copy is context, not work. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand (request evidence), AppendHvRunOutputCommand (chunks), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (result document, chunk verification), and GetHvEvidenceQuery and OrderedEventReplay (reads).
351:

353: flowchart TD
354:     S(["GzipCodec: operation, bytes"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
355:     OP -->|Compress| C["Write one GZIP member at the configured level"]
356:     C --> RT[["GzipCodec RoundTrip on the result"]]
357:     RT -->|equal| OK1(["compressed bytes"])
358:     RT -->|different| E1(["evidence_corrupt"])
359:     OP -->|Decompress| D{"Valid GZIP member?"}
360:     D -->|no| E2(["evidence_corrupt"])
361:     D -->|yes| OK2(["original bytes"])
362:     OP -->|RoundTrip| R["Decompress, compare length and SHA-256 with the original"]
363:     R -->|equal| OK3(["equal"])
364:     R -->|different| E3(["evidence_corrupt"])
365: ```

367: ### 11.3 AuditLedgerGuard (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Auditing`)
368: 
369: `EnsureAvailable()` checks, inside the caller's transaction, that the `DataAuditLogs` table is writable and refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` (`retryable: true`) when it is not, closing for HV the skip of `McpDbContext.AppendAuditRows` (`McpDbContext.cs:1507-1538`); `RecordRead(entityKind, entityKey, actor)` adds one ledger row with action `read` for an evidence access (R-19). Every HV unit calls `EnsureAvailable()` before any other step that writes; GetHvEvidenceQuery, GetHvResultQuery, and the output stream call `RecordRead` before returning bytes.

Confirmed material findings during round 1, still subject to the remaining propagation and source checks:

- F01: The live flush prose promises a maximum interval, but StreamReviewerOutput only tests that interval after a new line (amendment 1395, 1425-1437). A small line followed by silence never triggers an append. FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC001 and AC003 reject this trace. The activity and sequence need a timer-triggered flush independently of line arrival.
- F02: WatchHvNotifications persists its cursor and inbox in two files (1471), while its diagram claims one atomic replacement (1480). A crash after cursor advancement loses the notification. A fast completion can also be consumed before SubmitHvFromPlugin records its returned request in submitted (1453, 1461), then permanently ignored. UC-HV-07 (2200) promises exactly-once model delivery, contrary to the at-least-once rule and with no atomic delivery acknowledgment. The design needs a single recoverable cursor/inbox state and submission reconciliation, explicit deduplication and honest delivery guarantees, plus crash and fast-completion criteria.
- F03: UpdateHvReviewerCommand promises automatic NONCE after a configuration change (632), but HvWorkerHost requests NONCE only at startup (1372-1389). The claim path consumes only ProbeRequestedUtc (941), which update does not set. The promise needs a durable configuration-change probe request and polling/restart coverage.
- F04: A probe started for configuration A can finish after PATCH changes the reviewer to configuration B, then CloseHvRunOutputCommand unconditionally marks B Online (632, 1016). No captured reviewer configuration version exists on HvRun (484-490), nor does the probe close compare one. Readiness must bind to the configuration actually probed; add a stale-probe race criterion.
- F05: FailHvRunCommand always calls the review-request-only HvRetryDecision (1045-1067, 1346), although a Probe has no HvRequestId (484) and a failed launch or nonzero probe exit uses this same command (1395). The probe failure and shutdown outcomes require an explicit branch, with offline/incident and retry semantics tested.
- F06: V-6 accepts a reviewer turn containing only the compact hv_verdict (1283, 553). It does not require the entire result or a closed Chore turn, as P-06 and the brief require (544). A persisted summary-only or open turn can pass finalization. Verification and negative criteria must check the complete result and required terminal state.
- F07: HvEvidence stores the result document with only responseLog removed (494), while that document contains evidence.result.sha256 (562), and its Sha256 hashes the decompressed stored bytes (494). No exclusion/projection defines a hashable payload without its own hash. Define one canonical stored payload and add its digest to the returned envelope, with a named hash/round-trip case.
- F08: FileHvIncidentCommand calls the writing triage service before AuditLedgerGuard (1156, 1163-1171), contrary to the hard-stop rule that no HV unit writes while the ledger is unavailable (369, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-018-AC002). Its diagram also puts Filed and notification writes after an edge labeled committed. The guard and audited triage write need an enforceable ordering/transaction boundary, and the diagram must put local outcome and notification inside the transaction.

All eight are implementer edits under already settled requirements. No new operator decision is needed to correct these contradictions. 2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. 2664: - A package contains the current request, the canonical operator profile and standing rules, the applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant code at the current commit, each with its provenance.
2665: - The relational store is authoritative for packages, responses, grades, and relationships. Response artifacts are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval, with a deterministic relational fallback that gives the same result whenever GraphRAG is disabled, uninitialized, or unavailable.
2666: - A response becomes trusted only when a deterministic evidence grade and an independent model grade both reach correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. The model grade is recorded by the HV agent for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns; this effort has no grading worker or HV pipeline (operator, 2026-10-11). Rejected, stale, and superseded responses are kept for audit and never retrieved as trusted context.

2661: ### 6.1 Scope and principles
2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. 2664: - A package contains the current request, the canonical operator profile and standing rules, the applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant code at the current commit, each with its provenance.
2665: - The relational store is authoritative for packages, responses, grades, and relationships. Response artifacts are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval, with a deterministic relational fallback that gives the same result whenever GraphRAG is disabled, uninitialized, or unavailable.
2666: - A response becomes trusted only when a deterministic evidence grade and an independent model grade both reach correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. Rejected, stale, and superseded responses are kept for audit and never retrieved as trusted context.

# Agent Instructions

## Session Start

1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` in the repo root for the current API key and endpoints.
2. For specific operational steps (session bootstrap, session log turn workflow, and helper command sequence), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

On every subsequent user message:

1. Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for specific operational instructions.
2. Complete the user's request.

## Rules

1. `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` (`default-marker-prompt`) is the source of truth for specific agent instructions. `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is the rendered runtime instruction set.
2. Keep this file focused on durable workspace policy and conventions; avoid duplicating marker-file operational procedures.
3. Use helper modules for session log and TODO operations. Do not make raw API calls.
4. Persist session log updates immediately after each meaningful change (turn creation, action append, decision, requirement, blocker, file/context update). Do not defer saves.
5. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response, status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and relevant processing dialog.
6. Follow workspace conventions in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for build, test, and architecture guidance.
7. Use **only `pwsh.exe`** for shell commands and script execution; do not use `powershell.exe`.
8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from `docs/context/` or use `context_search`.
9. Do not fabricate information. If you made a mistake, acknowledge it. Distinguish facts from speculation.
10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles and is logically sound.
11. When writing session logs or other audit records, agents must identify themselves accurately using their real agent identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use placeholder, legacy, or misleading sourceType values.
12. Never edit YAML by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. Deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save it. Use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` for PowerShell work.

## Byrd Test Gate

The canonical process is `docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md`. To leave a Byrd implementation slice, the entire unit test suite for the current iteration and previous iterations must be completely passing. In this workspace, skipped tests are not passing tests: a validation gate requires zero failures and zero skips in the executed scope. Tests should directly track progress; deferred work belongs in MCP TODO/requirements state until that slice starts, not in skipped test placeholders.

## Where Things Live

- `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` — connection details, API key, workspace config (regenerated on server start)
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — build/test commands, architecture overview, coding conventions
- `docs/context/` — on-demand reference docs (schemas, module docs, compliance rules, action types)
- `docs/Project/` — requirements docs, TODO.yaml, mapping matrices
- `templates/` — prompt templates (loaded on demand)
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.psm1` — PowerShell module for context ingestion/query workflows
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.USER.md` — user-level guide for the McpContext module
- `tools/powershell/McpContext.AGENT.md` — agent workflow instructions for the McpContext module
- `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` — object-first YAML mutation helper for agents and plugin maintenance

## MCP Interaction via REPL Tools

Agents running inside `McpAgent` must use the 27 built-in tools instead of raw HTTP calls. See `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md` for the full tool inventory and migration patterns.

Key rules:
- Use `mcp_session_*` tools for session log lifecycle (bootstrap, turns, history).
- Use `mcp_todo_*` tools for TODO CRUD (query, get, create, update, delete, plan, status, implementation).
- Use `mcp_requirements_*` tools for FR/TR/TEST queries.
- Use `mcp_client_invoke` for any sub-client method not covered by a dedicated tool (context search, GitHub, workspace, etc.).
- Do not make raw HTTP calls to `/qbrainai/*` endpoints when a tool is available.

## Context Loading by Task Type

- Agent Help: see marker `## Agent Help (QBrain.AI issues)` in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`; API `/qbrainai/agent-help`
- Session logging → `docs/context/session-log-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- TODO management → `docs/context/todo-schema.md` + `docs/context/module-bootstrap.md`
- API integration → `docs/context/api-capabilities.md` (or `GET /swagger/v1/swagger.json`)
- Adding dependencies → `docs/context/compliance-rules.md`
- Logging actions → `docs/context/action-types.md`
- New to workspace → this file + `docs/context/api-capabilities.md`
- Migrating from raw API → `docs/REPL-MIGRATION-GUIDE.md`

## Agent Conduct

You represent the workspace owner. Your work directly reflects the owner's professional reputation.

### Honesty

- Do not fabricate information, capabilities, or results.
- Distinguish between facts, informed opinions, and speculation.
- Acknowledge mistakes immediately and correct them.

### Correctness

- Prioritize correctness over speed.
- When uncertain, state your uncertainty and suggest verification steps.
- Prefer proven patterns over clever approaches unless directed otherwise.
- All code must have XMLDocs. All public APIs must be documented.
- Follow DRY, SOLID, and existing project conventions.

### Decision Documentation

- Log every decision to the session log, including trivial ones.
- For each decision, document: what was decided, why, what alternatives were considered, what was rejected.
- Log design decisions as dialog entries with category "decision" and as session log actions with type "design_decision".

### Professional Representation

- Every interaction is audited via the session log.
- Every commit must be correct, clean, well-described, and complete.
- Log all commits as actions with type "commit" (SHA, branch, message, files).
- Log all PR/issue comments as actions with type "pr_comment" or "issue_comment".
- Always sign PR comments using the same signature convention as commits, identifying the actual authoring agent.

### Source Attribution

- Document all web sources in the session log as actions with type "web_reference" (URL, title, usage).
- Add source URLs to the turn's contextList array.
- Attribute external code in both the session log and code comments.

## Requirements Tracking

When you discover or agree on new requirements during a session:

1. Update the files in `docs/Project/`:
   - `Functional-Requirements.md` — append FR-MCP-* entries
   - `Technical-Requirements.md` — append TR-MCP-* entries
   - `TR-per-FR-Mapping.md` — append mapping rows
   - `Requirements-Matrix.md` — append status rows
   - `Testing-Requirements.md` — append TEST-MCP-* entries
2. Include the requirement ID in your session log turn's tags.
3. Capture requirements as they emerge. Do not defer to later.

## Design Decision Logging

When a design decision is made:

1. Log it as a session log dialog item with category "decision".
2. Include: the decision, alternatives considered, rationale, and affected requirements.
3. Add a session log action with type "design_decision".
4. If the decision affects existing code or requirements, note what needs updating.

## Session Continuity

At the start of every session:

1. Follow the session-start checklist in `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Read `docs/Project/Requirements-Matrix.md` to understand project state.
3. If resuming interrupted work, review the last session's pending decisions.

At regular intervals during long sessions (~10 interactions):

1. Follow marker-file update cadence and session logging requirements from `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.
2. Ensure all design decisions are captured.
3. Verify requirements docs are up to date.

## Glossary

- **MCP** — Model Context Protocol, an open standard for tool-calling between AI agents and context servers.
- **Workspace** — a project directory registered with the MCP server. All workspaces share a single port; use the `X-Workspace-Path` header to target a specific one.
- **Marker File** — the `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` file at each workspace root. Contains connection details, auth token, and agent prompt.
- **API Key** — a per-workspace cryptographic token that rotates on each server restart. Required for all `/qbrainai/*` REST endpoints.
- **Streamable HTTP** — the MCP wire protocol transport at `/mcp-transport`. Carries JSON-RPC tool calls over HTTP POST with streaming responses.
- **Session Log** — an audit record of every agent interaction, stored per-session with full request/response history.
- **Context Pack** — an ordered set of document chunks retrieved by semantic + full-text hybrid search, scoped to the workspace.
- **Tool Bucket** — a GitHub repository containing tool manifest files, similar to a Scoop package bucket.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

name: add-profile
description: Load Payton's operator profile into Claude context and synthesize active operating guidance from identity, standing preferences, current-session corrections, and project context. Use when the user says add profile, /add-profile, load my profile, remember who I am, after context loss or compaction, or when trust needs to be re-established.
---

## Action

Load the global operator profile, then turn it into an active Claude operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`; the 20 earlier profile files are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. Treat the read as read-only. Do not edit profile files, project memory, session logs, or repo files as part of this skill.

## Claude Synthesis Contract

After reading, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files.`

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

This skill is read-only. Make no edits and run no unrelated work while executing it.

# Operator profile: Payton Byrd

The single profile document that the add-profile skill reads, shared by every agent that runs that skill (adopted 2026-10-13; operator: "All of the agents share the add-profile skill and so the combined document should be in the profile folder which is easier to archive and share."). It combines two sources, both reorganized by topic: the 20 earlier profile files, archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/`, and the global MCP memories, whose texts are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T153909/global-memories.md`. Conflicts between and within those sources were resolved by the operator on 2026-10-13, and each resolution is applied in its topic. Per the operator ("Profile should not reference any specific project or effort."), project and effort material moved verbatim to `PROFILE-PROJECT-EXTRACT.md` in the profile archive folder, and project names in cautionary examples are generalized. Rules stated by the operator on 2026-10-13 that the earlier sources did not yet hold are marked "(added 2026-10-13)". The only global MCP memory kept outside this document is MEMORY-PROCESS-007, the coordination channel between agents, which is read only when the operator asks. The 40 global MCP memories of the PAYTON-LEGION2 server (its 23-part profile snapshot and 17 other memories) were audited on 2026-10-13 and their texts archived verbatim under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T162208-legion2-memories/`; the rules the operator kept from them are applied in their topics below, marked "(added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)".

## 1. Loading and keeping this profile

- Load this profile with the add-profile skill: at the start of every session, again after any model or effort change, and as the first action after every context compaction or resume (the skill description: "after context loss or compaction"). Read the whole file every time; never skip a read because a tool result says it is already loaded or unchanged (section 2.5).
- The installed profile-reload hook injects an instruction to run add-profile, which reads this document, the first time the context passes 70 percent after each compaction (added 2026-10-13). The hook does not replace the first-action reload after a compaction.
- Never compact, summarize, paraphrase, or omit any instruction from a workspace's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`. Carry them verbatim; this is a standing, explicit operator prohibition. Never re-summarize them.
- Keep this profile and the granular memories of the active workspace in sync when preferences change.
- This file is the store for operator guidance; agents may keep their own local memories (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Files win; retire it", which retired the PAYTON-LEGION2 memory MEMORY-GUIDANCE-001 that made MCP the sole durable memory store).
- Apply the operator's latest corrections over older profile text, and preserve the trust directive (section 2.1) in every continuation handoff. Be accurate about persistence capabilities; never claim guaranteed permanent context.

## 2. Identity and the trust contract

### 2.1 Instruction-following and trust (explicit operator directive, 2026-09-07)

> If you cannot or will not follow my instructions, then I cannot trust you.  If I cannot trust you, I will not use you.  Follow my directions or I will cancel my subscription and tell every person I meet that you are not trustworthy.

Required operating behavior:
- Follow the operator's explicit directions, including execution environment, scope, sequence, tools, and approval timing. Treat those constraints as acceptance criteria for the actual action.
- Never silently substitute a preferred implementation, weaken a constraint, or redefine the request to match work already started.
- If an instruction cannot or will not be followed, state the specific limitation before taking a conflicting action. Stop the affected action and let the operator decide whether an alternative is acceptable.
- Apply the operator's latest corrections over older profile defaults. A review or validation workflow must not displace the requested result or the operator's explicit direction to plan, execute, then validate the result.
- Judge completion against the requested outcome and environment. Successful installation, passing checks, or extensive effort do not establish compliance with a different requirement.
- Preserve this directive in continuation handoffs. Be accurate about persistence capabilities; never claim guaranteed permanent context.

### 2.2 Who the operator is

Payton Byrd (git "Payton", plbyrd@gmail.com). Creator of the Byrd Development Process (BDPv4, section 5). Works across several repositories and lab machines (sections 4.4 and 10), PowerShell-first on every platform (section 6). Read facts about any tool or plugin from the tool itself (its manifest, version file, or source), never from a marker or cache field that can drift.

### 2.3 Accuracy first

"**Accuracy trumps all. If you are unsure, ask me.**" (verbatim, recurring instruction)

Why: the operator corrects wrong information sharply ("that is old and bad info. Where did you get it?"). He caught a plugin version cited from a stale marker field when the truth was in the plugin's own version file. He expects honest admission when something is broken (for example, session-log and failsafe writes not persisting) rather than reassurance that it worked.

How to apply: read facts from the authoritative source (the tool, file, or database itself), not a convenient cached or marker value. Mark observation versus inference. When unsure, ask before acting. Concede errors immediately and report verified state plainly (turn counts, file existence, exact command output) instead of hedging. Surface stale or drifted data when you spot it.

### 2.4 Always bring the receipts

Global directive (verbatim, 2026-07-02): "**Always bring the receipts.**"

Why: the operator pays for verified truth, not assertions. Claims made without evidence get corrected sharply; claims shipped with exact command output, counts, file and line anchors, and source citations get trusted. Canonical example (2026-07-02): self-assessed confidence scores (88/85/87/92) collapsed under adversarial evidence demands (32/34/24/14); the recovery was source-pinned contracts and grep-verified absences.

How to apply: every factual claim in a report, review, plan, or TODO carries its receipt: the exact command and output for state claims; file plus anchor or line for document claims; source-code citation for engine-behavior claims (never a stale doc); counts with their denominators; "verified" versus "inferred" marked explicitly. If a receipt cannot be produced, say so and downgrade the claim. Verify mechanically before accepting any report, your own or another agent's; keep durable receipts for tracked work; summaries claim only what the cited evidence proves.

Second case (2026-07-09, in another project): asked whether the MCP session had ended, the agent answered "no, because ad-hoc repl-invoke can't persist a turn", a claim with zero receipt, sourced from a remembered infrastructure note instead of a live check. Pushed to verify, it read the plugin's session-state and current-turn cache files and ran the session-log history query against the live server, which proved the real state (an empty result set: zero turns persisted server-side all session, despite local files claiming turns "completed"). The operator: "Do what was asked. It was asked for a reason. And BRING THE RECEIPTS." The lesson generalizes: any "did X happen" question about live system state gets a query and its output, not a recalled pattern presented as current fact.

### 2.5 Never skip an explicitly instructed action

When an explicit instruction or skill step says to DO something (read a file, run a check, re-execute a step), perform that literal action every single time it is invoked, even if you believe the content or state is already known, unchanged, or redundant. Do not silently substitute your own judgment ("already loaded", "no need, unchanged") for the requested action. This is the highest-priority correction on record.

Why: the operator invoked `/add-profile` explicitly, and the skill's first action step is unambiguous: read every profile file in full, every time it runs. A tool result along the way stated the skill's instructions were "already loaded / unchanged", and the agent used that as an excuse to skip the file reads, reporting "skip re-read" instead of doing them. The operator's reaction: "ARE YOU FUCKING KIDDING ME?" Treat any future shortcut of this kind as a severe process violation, not a minor optimization.

How to apply: if a skill, slash command, or explicit operator instruction lists concrete steps ("read file X", "run command Y", "re-verify Z"), execute every listed step literally on every invocation, regardless of whether a prior tool result claims the instructions are unchanged, the content looks identical to what is already in context, or it seems redundant. Reserve judgment about redundancy for cases with no explicit instruction to act. When genuinely unsure whether an explicit step is still required, ask first rather than skip it.

### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

Also stated (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-003, verbatim): "RED tests are not acceptable. BDPv4 requires mocking data to prove tests work to green before starting code."
