1398: flowchart TD
1399:     S(["RunReviewerProcess: claim"]) --> B["Build the brief: accepted request in the run envelope, or the probe brief"]
1400:     B --> L[["Reviewer adapter BuildLaunch"]]
1401:     L --> ST{"Process started?"}
1402:     ST -->|no| FL[["FailHvRunCommand reviewer_launch_failed"]]
1403:     FL --> END1(["attempt ended"])
1404:     ST -->|yes| A1[["AppendHvRunOutputCommand: sequence 1, the hv_brief record"]]
1405:     A1 --> RUN[["StreamReviewerOutput: lines, flushes, heartbeats, until exit, stale fence, audit failure, or cancel"]]
1406:     RUN -->|"stale_fence or audit_unavailable"| K1["Kill the process"]
1407:     K1 --> END2(["attempt ended, no further write"])
1408:     RUN -->|"cancel requested"| K2["Kill the process"]
1409:     K2 --> FC[["FailHvRunCommand canceled"]]
1410:     FC --> END3(["attempt ended: request Canceled"])
1411:     RUN -->|"exited"| FLS[["AppendHvRunOutputCommand: remaining lines, then the adapter's hv_provenance lines"]]
1412:     FLS --> EX{"Exit code 0?"}
1413:     EX -->|no| FN[["FailHvRunCommand reviewer_exited_nonzero"]]
1414:     FN --> END4(["attempt ended"])
1415:     EX -->|yes| CO[["CloseHvRunOutputCommand"]]

1418:     CO -->|"Probe: passed or failed"| END6(["attempt ended: reviewer Online or Offline"])

1440: ### 16.3 Reviewer adapter contract [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-001, -003, -008]
1441: 
1442: `IHvReviewerAdapter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.HostileValidation.Reviewers`), one implementation per reviewer id:
1443: 
1444: - `BuildLaunch(brief, reviewer)`: a `ProcessStartInfo` built as an argument list, never a shell string, with the brief on standard input or in a temporary file the adapter deletes after the run; the launch arguments come from one shared launch builder that develop's one-shot strategy also uses, so the per-CLI arguments of `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy` (`AddCodexArguments`, `AddClaudeArguments`, `AddGrokArguments`, `AddClineArguments`, `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:238-262`) are written once (DRY); processes start through the existing `IProcessSpawner` and `IProcessEnvironmentService` (`OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:18-21`). The shared launch builder holds the one table of highest efforts of section 10 (P9). The reviewer runs behind a write barrier verified for its CLI (VI-03, probes of 2026-10-16): Codex `exec -s read-only` (a write attempt was refused by its sandbox), Grok `--permission-mode plan` (a write call was refused; a headless Grok run then ends `cancelled` at the first call that needs approval, so its launch allows the read tools a review uses), and Copilot `--available-tools` naming only read tools (write and shell tools are not offered at all). Claude's and Cline's plan modes are not accepted as barriers on that evidence (Claude's model declined before its barrier was exercised; Cline ran a shell command in plan mode), so Claude's launch restricts its tools structurally (`--tools`) and Cline stays unqualified until H1 proves a barrier. Whether each reviewer's plugin can still log its turn behind its barrier (the plugin writes host-session state and calls the server) is verified in H1 (VI-03, VI-04); a reviewer that cannot fails its NONCE (R-24).
1445: - Live lines (R-12, P8): standard output and standard error are read line by line as the process writes them (asynchronous line reads on the redirected streams), and each line is handed to the run's callback at once; nothing waits for the process to end.
1446: - `NormalizeLine(line, stream)`: a native JSON event line of a CLI run in a JSON streaming mode is kept as written; any other line becomes `{ "type": "hv_raw", "stream", "line" }`.
1447: - `ExtractReviewerRecords(lines)`: one pure function over a run's ordered native lines. It assembles each agent message's complete text by the CLI's event model (Grok's per-token `text` events, Copilot's `assistant.message_delta` events followed by the whole `assistant.message`, Claude's whole assistant messages, Codex's `agent_message` items, Cline's accumulated content) and returns, in message order, every line of that text that is exactly one JSON object of a reviewer record type of section 13.3; the fence lines of a fenced block are ignored, and a line holding other text beside a record is free text. The worker runs it as lines arrive and passes each batch's completed records to AppendHvRunOutputCommand; finalization runs it over the stored log; both get the same records (R-12). Record types the worker writes itself (`hv_brief`, `hv_provenance`, `hv_raw`) are never accepted from message text, so a reviewer cannot forge them.
1448: - `ReadProvenance(run)`: `hv_provenance` lines read from the CLI's own runtime receipt after the run (P-04), sources verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): for Codex, the thread's rollout `turn_context` (fields `model` and `effort`; observed `model` `gpt-6-astra`, `effort` `max`), the source the foundation's `runtime_identity` check reads (foundation section 6.3, check 8); for Claude, the session transcript under `~/.claude/projects` (the assistant message `model` and the request `effort`), written only when session persistence is on, so the launch never passes `--no-session-persistence`; for Grok, the session store `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<sessionId>/` (`summary.json` `reasoning_effort`, and a model id that `chat_history.jsonl` names `grok-4.7-build` while the events name `grok-4.7`, so H1 pins the field V-7 compares); for Copilot, the run's own JSON stream (each call's `assistant.message.model` and `user.message.responsesReasoning.effort`; `--usage-output-file` holds the model only); for Cline, none, because its run records hold the model and only whether thinking was on, so V-7 and the NONCE fail closed (L-04, D-06).
1449: - Highest effort when none is configured: the verified values of section 10 (VI-08), never develop's one-shot constants (P9).

1451: ### 16.4 Process SubmitHvFromPlugin: the plugin verb [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-005, -020]
1452: 
1453: `workflow.hv.submit` in the PowerShell core (`plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1`): process BindVerbToTurn (foundation section 4.4) binds the invocation to its turn; the verb sends SubmitHvRequestCommand through the REPL with `submitter` that turn's key and `idempotencyKey` `hv-<requestId>-<first 16 hex of the SHA-256 of the scope and context>`, so a repeat of the same call is the same request. A created or stored request is recorded in `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-notifications.yaml` (`submitted`) for the watcher (section 16.5) and reported with its id, status, and reviewer. `hv_no_reviewer_available` is reported with the context S-16 asks for: each reviewer's enabled flag, readiness, and reason from `details.reviewers`, the open incident of each `Offline` reviewer (through `workflow.hv.incidents`), and the remedy text "after the cause is fixed, NONCE the reviewer: workflow.hv.nonce <reviewerId>". Every other refusal is reported with its code, final. A retryable answer (transport outage, 503, 409 with `retryable: true`) is reported with `retryable: true` and exit 1 and is not queued in the failsafe, because the same call with the same key can simply be repeated (the reviews' no-failsafe rule, foundation section 5.2).

1455: ```mermaid
1456: flowchart TD
1457:     S(["workflow.hv.submit: scope, context"]) --> B[["Process BindVerbToTurn"]]
1458:     B -->|refused| E1(["refusal of BindVerbToTurn, drawn there"])
1459:     B -->|bound turn| K["Submitter the bound turn key; idempotencyKey from requestId, scope, and context"]
1460:     K --> SUB["REPL: SubmitHvRequestCommand"]
1461:     SUB -->|"201 or 200"| REC["Record the hvRequestId in hv-notifications.yaml submitted"]
1462:     REC --> R1(["reported: id, status, reviewer"])
1463:     SUB -->|"409 hv_no_reviewer_available"| CTX["Add reviewer statuses, open incidents, and the NONCE remedy"]
1464:     CTX --> R2(["reported: refusal with context, exit 1"])
1465:     SUB -->|"retryable answer"| R3(["reported: code, retryable true, exit 1, not queued"])
1466:     SUB -->|"other refusal"| R4(["reported: code, final, exit 1"])
1467: ```

1469: ### 16.5 Process WatchHvNotifications: completions into the plugin [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-017, -020]
1470: 
1471: Started by process StartHostSession (foundation section 4.4) for each host session and stopped by EndHostSession; one instance per host session (`sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-watcher.pid`, the arrival bridge's pattern). It runs the REPL streaming verb `workflow.hv.watchNotifications` with `Last-Event-ID` the `lastSequence` of `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-notifications.yaml`. For each event it records `lastSequence` and, when the event is `hv_completed`, `hv_failed`, or `hv_canceled` for a request in `submitted`, appends it to `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/hv-inbox.yaml`; each write is one atomic replace (temp file, flush, rename) under `hv-notifications.lock`. A disconnect reconnects with backoff from the recorded sequence, so nothing is missed (R-16). The prompt hook adds each undelivered inbox entry once to the next prompt's context ("HV <hvRequestId> <status>, overall verdict <verdict>; result: workflow.hv.result <hvRequestId>") and marks it delivered. Plugins never call REST; the REPL holds the stream (R-30).

1485:     BK --> C
1486:     E -->|"host session ended"| END(["stopped"])

1489: ### 16.6 Director HV commands [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-020]
1490: 
1491: The Director commands of section 13.1 run through `IHostileValidationDirectorExecutor` in `src/QBrainAi.Cqrs.Mvvm/HostileValidationDirectorCommands.cs`, the pattern of the existing hostile-review Director commands (`src/QBrainAi.Cqrs.Mvvm/HostileReviewDirectorCommands.cs:22`); `hv-output` and `hv-notifications` consume the client streams and reconnect from their last event id; `hv-submit` submits as `Operator` with the operator's name (R-09). 164: - R-22 Verdict only (S-25). No HV unit writes TODO state. A result names the reviewed turns' `todoId` values for information only.
165: - R-23 Requirement references (S-14). The submitted context is stored as written (Markdown, YAML, or text, declared by `contextFormat`) and parsed for requirement references: FR, TR, and TEST ids of the form `<KIND>-<AREA>-<NNN>` with optional further dash-separated area segments, acceptance criteria written as `<FR id>-AC<NNN>` or `<FR id> ac-<n>`, and use cases by their store id or exact title. Each reference is resolved against the workspace's effective requirements and use cases and handed to the reviewer as a delineated list with its resolution status; an unresolved reference is listed as unresolved, never refused (shared component RequirementReferenceExtractor).
166: - R-24 The reviewer's own turn (P-06). The brief tells the reviewer to log its review as its own session-log turn, classified `Chore` so that its turn never needs an HV of its own (foundation completion policy: Chore needs no hostile review), and to store its entire result there. Finalization requires that turn to exist, to be persisted (not a failsafe or queued record), to have been created after the run started, and to contain the run's `hv_verdict` record byte for byte in its stored normal form (V-6). A reviewer whose host cannot log turns fails its NONCE with `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported`. The reviewer's plugin runs as a host session of its own: a review or probe run never reads or changes the plugin state or the session-log session of a live session of the same agent in the workspace (FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC008), which matters because a reviewer starts in the workspace (section 16.2) and Grok's headless hooks write their host state under the working directory's `.mcpServer/grok/` (VI-04).
167: - R-25 The HostileReview subsystem stays separate. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-001 to -006 (its queue, artifact links, findings, and query surface) are not changed by this amendment, as the foundation already states (foundation section 5.4); the problems found in it (section 21, P1 to P3) are tracked in REMED-HVPIPELINE-001. It stays separate (D-02, settled): it reviews artifacts (TODO, FR/TR/TEST, plans, files, commits; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002) while this pipeline reviews session turns (S-03), the approved foundation keeps it separate, and consolidating it is scope the operator has not named. Its missing worker (P1) is built on this amendment's execution components (process HvWorkerHost and the reviewer adapters), so reviewer execution exists once (the DRY ruling).
168: - R-26 Scope limits. One request names turns of one MCP session. `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, the foundation's `HvRequest:MaxTurns` default) bounds every scope; a session scope above it is refused with 400 `hv_scope_too_large` naming the count, never truncated.
169: - R-27 One open review per turn. A turn is `Pending` in at most one open request (a unique filtered index on the turn key where the item is `Pending`); admission over a pending turn is refused with 409 `hv_turns_pending` naming the turns and their requests, and over a final turn with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed` (S-06, S-20).
170: - R-28 Cancellation by anyone (S-18). `Queued` becomes `Canceled` at once; `Running` becomes `CancelRequested`, and the worker stops the process at its next heartbeat and closes the run `Canceled`; `Finalizing`, `Completed`, `Failed`, and `Canceled` refuse with 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable`. 2: 
3: - F01: The live flush prose promises a maximum interval, but StreamReviewerOutput only tests that interval after a new line (amendment 1395, 1425-1437). A small line followed by silence never triggers an append. FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC001 and AC003 reject this trace. The activity and sequence need a timer-triggered flush independently of line arrival.
4: - F02: WatchHvNotifications persists its cursor and inbox in two files (1471), while its diagram claims one atomic replacement (1480). A crash after cursor advancement loses the notification. A fast completion can also be consumed before SubmitHvFromPlugin records its returned request in submitted (1453, 1461), then permanently ignored. UC-HV-07 (2200) promises exactly-once model delivery, contrary to the at-least-once rule and with no atomic delivery acknowledgment. The design needs a single recoverable cursor/inbox state and submission reconciliation, explicit deduplication and honest delivery guarantees, plus crash and fast-completion criteria.
5: - F03: UpdateHvReviewerCommand promises automatic NONCE after a configuration change (632), but HvWorkerHost requests NONCE only at startup (1372-1389). The claim path consumes only ProbeRequestedUtc (941), which update does not set. The promise needs a durable configuration-change probe request and polling/restart coverage.
6: - F04: A probe started for configuration A can finish after PATCH changes the reviewer to configuration B, then CloseHvRunOutputCommand unconditionally marks B Online (632, 1016). No captured reviewer configuration version exists on HvRun (484-490), nor does the probe close compare one. Readiness must bind to the configuration actually probed; add a stale-probe race criterion.
7: - F05: FailHvRunCommand always calls the review-request-only HvRetryDecision (1045-1067, 1346), although a Probe has no HvRequestId (484) and a failed launch or nonzero probe exit uses this same command (1395). The probe failure and shutdown outcomes require an explicit branch, with offline/incident and retry semantics tested.
8: - F06: V-6 accepts a reviewer turn containing only the compact hv_verdict (1283, 553). It does not require the entire result or a closed Chore turn, as P-06 and the brief require (544). A persisted summary-only or open turn can pass finalization. Verification and negative criteria must check the complete result and required terminal state.
9: - F07: HvEvidence stores the result document with only responseLog removed (494), while that document contains evidence.result.sha256 (562), and its Sha256 hashes the decompressed stored bytes (494). No exclusion/projection defines a hashable payload without its own hash. Define one canonical stored payload and add its digest to the returned envelope, with a named hash/round-trip case.
10: - F08: FileHvIncidentCommand calls the writing triage service before AuditLedgerGuard (1156, 1163-1171), contrary to the hard-stop rule that no HV unit writes while the ledger is unavailable (369, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-018-AC002). Its diagram also puts Filed and notification writes after an edge labeled committed. The guard and audited triage write need an enforceable ordering/transaction boundary, and the diagram must put local outcome and notification inside the transaction.
11: 
12: All eight are implementer edits under already settled requirements. No new operator decision is needed to correct these contradictions. The 63 records and 114 acceptance criteria compare equal field by field; there are 21 mapping groups represented by 42 store edges. The 78 probe files match the manifest. Do not change the store to fit the claim.

The request must be Open in the retained foundation contract, but finalization calls it while Finalizing. The old DTO still requires removed receipt paths and thread fields; its pre-write staleness dispatch expects no transaction, whereas the new call is inside one. Replace the complete internal grade contract, guards, side effects, and diagrams, including responsibility for completing the outer request. A-09 also names section 3.1 for a check actually in 6.3 (foundation 2842).
+- F11: The response finding wire shape (551) has only claimId, check, outcome, whereas V-8 (1285) requires category, location, evidence and remediation on every finding. HvFinding (498) has no response scope or response id, and the result's responseGrades omit findings (562) while its failures promise every FAIL and UNKNOWN (564). Define a lossless response finding contract and result projection, with negative tests for missing remediation and positive failing-grade persistence.
+- F12: ResponseStatusTransition may close a Pending response during review (182, 480; FR-MCP-HVPIPE-021-AC003), while the accepted request is immutable (544). V-3/V-8 bind against the current Pending set (1280, 1285). A reviewer legitimately grading the admitted response after it closes is rejected and taken Offline. Bind reviewer output to the accepted set and define how closed items are ignored at commit, with reject/supersede races covered.
+- F13: V-4 makes overall AGREE an iff over holistic and turn verdicts, omitting response grades (1281), while importing the foundation verdict_match iff over response grades (foundation 2840). These rules disagree for mixed turn/response outcomes and R-31 forbids every FAIL/UNKNOWN (173). Define one overall predicate over all applicable verdicts and findings and propagate it to the foundation replacement and criteria.
+- F14: No unit persists HvRun StartedUtc, ProcessId or the Claimed-to-Running transition. The run declares these fields (486), V-6 and ReadinessProbeVerdict use StartedUtc, Claim only starts the request (941), heartbeat only renews it (971), and RunReviewerProcess starts the OS process without a fenced run-start write (1395-1405). Define the owning command and its ordering/crash outcomes, with start/provenance tests.
+- F15: Cancel can commit CancelRequested after the last heartbeat and before successful process exit; CloseHvRunOutputCommand then overwrites it with Finalizing without checking cancellation (1016). This loses an accepted cancellation. R-28 also refuses repeat cancel of Canceled (170), while CancelHvRequestCommand returns 200 for it (787). Define consistent repeat semantics and the serialized cancel/close/finalize outcomes, with each interleaving tested.
+- F16: RemoveHvEvidenceCommand writes RemovedBy and RemovalReason to output chunks (859, 873), but their entity has neither field (492). GetHvRequestQuery's lastOutput and StreamHvRunOutputQuery still decompress removed payloads without a removed-evidence outcome (753, 880-893), unlike FR-MCP-HVPIPE-019-AC004. Define the retained fields and post-removal behavior on every payload-reading surface, with named cases.
+- F17: VI-05's asserted maximum of 14400 appends per run hour (2500) is false under R-12 and the byte-triggered flush (1395): multiple OutputFlushBytes batches can arrive within one interval. State a valid measurement workload and account for byte-triggered writes and audit overhead; do not call this an interval-imposed bound.
+- F18: H3 promises P1 to P3 fixed using HvWorkerHost (167, 2486), but the host and claim/failure/finalization contracts only service HvRequest. The live FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 AC4 separately requires configured/default AgentPool behavior, distinct request/attempt/pool-job/model-execution/accepted-result identities, internal-only cancellation and one accepted terminal result. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 AC4 prohibits raw artifact/prompt storage, unlike turn HV's complete brief log. No artifact queue adapter, units, identity mapping, retention boundary, or tests integrate these unchanged requirements. Define that separate-context contract and its H0 mocks/H3 production cases before approval, sharing only compatible execution primitives.
+- F19: W-03 and sequence 17.7 assume the reviewer process is gone when the worker crashes (298, 1870). The reused IProcessSpawner starts an ordinary process and provides explicit Kill only (DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51). A killed worker cannot call Kill or observe stale_fence; lease expiry fences database writes but does not stop its child. No owner-death containment or recovery outcome is specified. Define and test abrupt worker death with a surviving reviewer and descendants, without imposing a review deadline.
+- F20: The plugin idempotency key embeds the full requestId plus a fixed 20-character prefix/suffix overhead (1453), but requestId may be 256 and IdempotencyKey only 128 (453, 471). A valid requestId above 108 characters produces an invalid key. It also omits the full submitting session identity and contextFormat, although the payload fingerprint includes them. Define a bounded canonical key over the full invocation identity and test maximum-length and cross-session calls.
+- F21: A late verification failure can overwrite successful finalization. FailHvRunCommand accepts null WorkerId and the released stored fence (1045), checks only FencedLease, and writes Failed plus request retry state (1046). Finalize may commit Succeeded/Completed first (1100) without changing that released fence. Unlike finalization, Fail does not re-check OutputClosed/Finalizing and versions in its transaction. A finalizer that read the earlier state can therefore undo completion. Add state/version-conditional failure acceptance and idempotent terminal behavior, with a concurrent success/verification-failure test.
+
+All F09 through F21 are implementer edits under existing requirements. No operator choice is needed to decide whether these contracts must be made consistent.
+
+- U01: Nine signed effort commits and eight adjacent recorded push transitions are verified linear and fast-forward. A reflog's update-by-push message does not prove which flags were used. The absolute claim that every push used no force flag needs the original push command/output or a server audit. Do not invent that evidence.
+- U02: The catalog has named tests for all 114 FR acceptance criteria, but no complete real-binding AC-to-phase allocation is supplied. In particular, H1 owns live reviewer/plugin qualification while the worker arrives H3 and streams H6; H5 watcher and H6 stream delivery are parallel, with no explicit activation/rollback contract. Component mocks can be correct, but they do not prove that these production acceptance cases can run in the owning phase. Provide the exact phase and prerequisite binding for each criterion and distinguish H1 adapter tests from later server-launched/live-stream cases. This is an evidence/plan edit, not a request to lower or waive a gate.
+
+Validator process disclosure: one broad rg command accidentally scanned outside the intended source paths, including local projections. No result from it was used as TODO or requirement evidence. The inspector now rejects rg calls without an explicit permitted source path. The earlier credential extraction error, its redaction, and the limitation that prior tool output cannot be withdrawn remain disclosed in hv-r1-process-correction.md. These are my errors and are not scored as implementer conduct.
*** End Patch"));

290: - L-04 A reviewer CLI that cannot report its runtime model and effort cannot pass a NONCE, so it stays `Unverified` or `Offline` (R-10, P-04). Verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-01): Codex, Claude, Grok, and Copilot record both in their own run records; Cline records the model and only whether thinking was on, never the effort level, so Cline cannot pass a NONCE until it records the effort of a run (D-06, settled: P-04 fails closed).

292: ## 9. Crash windows and recovery
293: 
294: Each window names what is durable at the crash and what recovers it. "Sweep" is the worker host's periodic pass (process HvWorkerHost).
295: 
296: - W-01 Crash after the submit commit, before the worker wakes: the request is `Queued` in the store; the next poll claims it.
297: - W-02 Crash after a claim, before the process starts: the run's lease expires; the sweep marks the attempt `Abandoned` and the request `Queued`, or `Failed` or `Canceled` with its turns released when its attempts are spent or a cancel was requested (ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand, policy HvRetryDecision).
298: - W-03 Worker crash while the reviewer runs: the reviewer's output pipe closes with the worker; the output already appended is durable; the lease expires and the sweep queues a new attempt. A worker that is alive but lost its lease (a pause longer than the lease) gets `stale_fence` on its next write and stops its process (I-05).
299: - W-04 Crash after the reviewer exits, before CloseHvRunOutputCommand commits: as W-03, a new attempt runs (L-02).
300: - W-05 Crash after CloseHvRunOutputCommand commits (request `Finalizing`), before finalization: the sweep dispatches FinalizeHvRequestCommand for every `Finalizing` request (idempotent, I-03).
301: - W-06 Crash or failure inside the finalization transaction: it rolls back; the request stays `Finalizing` and the sweep runs finalization again.
302: - W-07 Crash after the finalization commit, before any stream delivers its notification: the notification row is durable; streams and pollers replay it by sequence (R-16).
303: - W-08 Crash after an incident row commits, before triage filing: the incident stays `Pending`; the sweep files it (FileHvIncidentCommand).
304: - W-09 Crash after triage accepts a filing, before the report id is recorded: the retry files again under the same `dedupeKey`, which joins the same triage group (L-03).
305: - W-10 Cancel racing finalization, claim, or close: all of them change the request row inside SerializableWrite, so one commits first and the other sees the committed state (R-28).
306: - W-11 Two workers claiming one request: the claim is a conditional update on the request's state and version inside SerializableWrite; exactly one claim commits.
307: - W-12 The audit ledger becomes unavailable during a run: AppendHvRunOutputCommand refuses with 503 `audit_unavailable` and writes nothing; the worker stops the reviewer process (a hard stop, S-29), cannot record the failure while the ledger is down, and the lease expiry later queues a new attempt; nothing is ever reported complete without its audit rows.
308: 
309: ## 10. Configuration: `HostileValidationOptions`
310: 
311: Section `Mcp:HostileValidation`, declared under the canonical root as `QBrainAi: HostileValidation:` in `appsettings.yaml` and projected onto `Mcp:` by `CanonicalSectionProjectionProvider`, as foundation section 6.2 declares `AgentContext`; class `HostileValidationOptions` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/HostileValidation/HostileValidationOptions.cs` with `SectionName = "Mcp:HostileValidation"`, `Validate()`, and `ValidateOnStart()`; per instance through `McpInstanceResolver`.
312: 
313: - `Reviewers` (list): exactly one entry for each of `Cline`, `Copilot`, `Claude`, `Codex`, and `Grok` (S-02); each entry has `Enabled` (default true), `ExecutionStrategy` (an existing strategy name, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/IAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:6-46`), `AgentPath` (the CLI to launch), `Model` (null means the CLI's default model, recorded from the runtime provenance; Copilot needs a configured model, because its default `auto` routes each prompt to a model of its own choosing, which two probe prompts of 2026-10-16 showed by landing on `mai-code-1.1-flash` and `gpt-6-luna`, and it refuses `--reasoning-effort` without an explicit model, so V-7 could not hold, VI-02), `Effort` (null means the highest effort the reviewer's CLI accepts, verified on 2026-10-16 (VI-08): Codex `max` (its rollout recorded `effort` `max`), Claude `max` (its transcript recorded `effort` `max`), Cline `xhigh` (the highest `--thinking` level), Grok `xhigh` (Grok 1.0.60 refuses `max`: "unknown effort level 'max'; use one of: xhigh, high, medium, low"), and Copilot `max` (the highest `--reasoning-effort` value, which the configured model's NONCE proves); develop's one-shot constants at `OneShotCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs:23-26` differ for Codex (`xhigh`) and Grok (`max`, which Grok refuses), problem P9), and `MaxConcurrentRuns` (default 1, 1..8).
314: - `MaxTurnsPerRequest` (default 200, 1..2000).
315: - `MaxAttemptsPerRequest` (default 3, 1..10).
316: - `LeaseDuration` (default 5 minutes) and `HeartbeatInterval` (default 60 seconds; must be less than half of `LeaseDuration`).
317: - `OutputFlushInterval` (default 250 milliseconds, 50..5000) and `OutputFlushBytes` (default 65536, 1024..4194304); the default interval is kept only after its storage cost is measured (VI-05).
318: - `PollInterval` (default 2 seconds) and `WorkerEnabled` (default true).
319: - There is no execution timeout and no output size limit (R-11, S-22: "Output should be captured live and streamed").
320: - Startup validation fails on an unknown or duplicate reviewer id, a missing one of the five, an unknown execution strategy, an enabled Copilot entry without a configured `Model`, or a value outside its range.
321: - Seeding: at startup each reviewer entry is inserted as an `HvReviewer` row when the workspace has none for its id (readiness `Unverified`); an existing row is never overwritten, because UpdateHvReviewerCommand is the real-time management surface (S-02), the pattern develop uses for agent definitions seeded per workspace (`SeedWorkspaceAgentsAsync`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/IAgentPoolService.cs:83`).
322: 
323: ## 11. Shared components (new, each defined once)
324: 
325: The foundation's shared components (foundation section 3.5) are reused unchanged: SerializableWrite, IdempotentCreate with PayloadFingerprint, ReadableKeyAllocator, PagedQuery with PageBounds, ClassifiedErrorException with ErrorCodes, SecretRedactor, ContentHasher, TurnLocator, TurnWritePipeline, ScoreLexeme, ScoreVerdict, and WorkspaceResolutionBehavior. The components below are new; each has one implementation, one test class named for it, and one diagram here, and every unit that uses one draws it as a single call node.
326: 
327: ### 11.1 FencedLease (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Leases`)
328: 
329: Claims, renews, and takes over the lease of one row, and guards every fenced write, following develop's handoff-ingestion pattern (`HandoffIngestionService.cs:724-735,782-807`). Operations: `Claim(row, owner, duration)` (only when the row has no lease or an expired one; the fence token increments), `Renew(row, owner, fence, duration)`, `Guard(row, owner, fence)` (the precondition of every fenced write), `Release(row, owner, fence)`. Each runs inside the caller's SerializableWrite. Used by ClaimHvRunCommand, RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand, AppendHvRunOutputCommand, CloseHvRunOutputCommand, FailHvRunCommand, and ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand.
330: 
331: ```mermaid
332: flowchart TD
333:     S(["FencedLease: operation, row, owner, fence"]) --> OP{"Operation?"}
334:     OP -->|Claim| CL{"Lease absent or expired?"}
335:     CL -->|no| E1(["held: another owner holds a live lease"])
336:     CL -->|yes| CT["Set owner and expiry, increment the fence token"]
337:     CT --> OK1(["claimed: the new fence token"])
338:     OP -->|"Renew, Guard, or Release"| G{"Owner and fence equal the stored ones?"}
339:     G -->|no| E2(["stale_fence: nothing changed"])
340:     G -->|yes| W{"Operation?"}
341:     W -->|Renew| RN["Extend the expiry"]
342:     RN --> OK2(["renewed"])
343:     W -->|Guard| OK3(["guarded: the caller's write proceeds"])
344:     W -->|Release| RL["Clear owner and expiry"]
345:     RL --> OK4(["released"])
346: ```
347: 
348: ### 11.2 GzipCodec (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Compression`)
349: 
350: `Compress(bytes)` returns one GZIP member; `Decompress(bytes)` returns the original bytes; `RoundTrip(original, compressed)` decompresses and compares length and SHA-256 (through ContentHasher's hex form over raw bytes) and fails with `evidence_corrupt` on any difference, so no compressed blob is stored unverified. It follows `DataAuditLogEntity`'s encode and decode (`DataAuditLogEntity.cs:119-147`); that entity's private copy is context, not work. Used by SubmitHvRequestCommand (request evidence), AppendHvRunOutputCommand (chunks), FinalizeHvRequestCommand (result document, chunk verification), and GetHvEvidenceQuery and OrderedEventReplay (reads).

938: #### ClaimHvRunCommand: claim the next probe or review [FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003, -007]
939: 
940: - Handler: `ClaimHvRunCommand(string WorkspacePath, string WorkerId) : ICommand<HvRunClaim?>`; `HvRunClaim { runId, kind, reviewerId, attempt, fenceToken, leaseExpiresUtc, hvRequestId, expectedModel, expectedEffort, probeNonce }`.
941: - Delegate: AuditLedgerGuard; then, in this order: (1) a probe: the first enabled reviewer, in pool order, with `ProbeRequestedUtc` set and fewer active runs than its `MaxConcurrentRuns`: insert its `Probe` run (`hvprobe-` key, a fresh 32-byte random `ProbeNonce` in lower-case hex), FencedLease `Claim`, clear `ProbeRequestedUtc`; (2) otherwise a review: the oldest `Queued` request (by `CreatedUtc`, then `HvRequestId`) whose assignee is eligible with capacity, or whose assignee is no longer eligible and for which policy RoundRobinAssignment finds an eligible reviewer with capacity (the reassignment is recorded on the request); insert its `Review` run (`hvrun-<hvRequestId>-<nn>`, `Attempt` = `AttemptCount` + 1), FencedLease `Claim`, set the request `Running` (with `StartedUtc` on the first attempt) and `AttemptCount` + 1, and append `hv_started`. With nothing claimable it returns null and writes nothing; a request whose turns are all frozen stays `Queued` while no reviewer is eligible (ETA `Unknown`, R-18).
942: - Concurrency: the request's state, version, and the one-live-run index are checked and written in the delegate, so two workers never claim one request (W-11).
943: - Results: a claim; null; 409 `conflict` (`retryable: true`, the worker tries again at its next poll); 503 `audit_unavailable`.
